waypoints.title: fence FIFO admission: DESIGN the WAIT-line protocol (implementation split to W47)
waypoints.next_bounded_step: None -- this waypoint is done. See W47.
waypoints.evidence: 2026-09-26: 2026-09-26 MEASURED LIVE (W38), scratch ledger under /var/tmp, never the real ledger: fixture TOTAL_MB 100 + a dead LEASE (pid 999999) + WAIT bbbb 8888:1 <epoch> 50 blocked-job. (1) GC KEEPS a WAIT line verbatim: membudget status (which runs ensure then gc under lock) reaped the dead LEASE but left the WAIT line byte-identical, because membudget-ledger's gc() case-matches only 'LEASE *' (membudget-ledger:109) and falls through everything else, WAIT included, to the unconditional keep branch (line 121) — no liveness check ever runs on it, confirmed by the dead WAIT owner (8888:1) surviving. (2) ADMISSION IGNORES it completely: MEMBUDGET_NOBLOCK=1 membudget run 85 probe-job admitted instantly, reporting 'global free was 100MB' — the WAIT line's 50MB was never subtracted. Root cause read at source: _snapshot() (scripts/membudget:105-110) awk-sums only dollar1==TOTAL_MB and dollar1==LEASE; no code path anywhere in cmd_run reads a WAIT line for budget, ordering, or anything else. Conclusion: any WAIT-line design is safe to introduce (gc will carry it) but is COMPLETELY INERT on the bash side until bash's admission is taught to read it — FIFO holds only once both clients honour the line, exactly as queue.md predicted. | 2026-09-26: 2026-09-26 DESIGNED: a Waiter dataclass mirrors Lease's 7-field ledger shape -- WAIT ticket mb owner epoch parent label -- so parse/gc/render reuse the same word-count and liveness machinery leases already have, instead of treating a WAIT line as opaque extra forever. Semantics, chosen after W38's measurement: STRICT head-of-line FIFO, not any-waiter-that-currently-fits -- admission proceeds only when the verdict is ADMIT for this request AND either no live waiters exist or this request's own ticket is the oldest live one, so a later smaller request can never overtake an earlier larger one even when it would itself fit right now. That is exactly the failure summit's witness measured (later arrival B admitted ahead of waiting A) and the only reading of 'arrival-order admission' that actually closes it -- the weaker any-that-fits reading would still starve A behind an endless stream of small Bs. Dead waiters are reaped by gc using the SAME is_alive predicate as leases, no cascade (a waiter has no children). A WAIT line is appended on first BLOCK and removed atomically with either the LEASE append (same locked section) or a terminal refusal/give-up, so no window exists where a ticket is queued but nothing will ever clear it. Split into W47 (implement in admit.py, one commit), W48 (letter to substrate; bash's own side stays inert per W38 until it lands its own patch), W49 (tell summit and amr-skills).

waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-01: inventory measured: 13 distributions, 0 cross-distribution imports (ast over src and tests; positive control 436 same-distribution imports), so all coupling is shared infra (MODULE.bazel 31 hubs, venv.bzl, check drivers, .githooks, 3 cross-package hooks tests, SKELETON/INSTALL). Plan and order in .claude/design/W317-split-plan.md | 2026-10-01: believed operator-directed (no record found; original attached) 2026-10-01: one-version rule's PURPOSE (agents stay current) must survive -> pin-bump bot + fleet staleness census, D4 withdrawn; per-repo gates on GitHub Actions (free for public repos); cross-package tests atomized (step 0 minted as W318). mtools is already PUBLIC (gh repo view), so the split publishes nothing new | 2026-10-01: operator 2026-10-01: keep agents current via a meta package and/or >= floors set whenever something is built on a consumer's behalf. Plan takes both (floors = correctness, meta = freshness); both need real semver per module, so release publishing is decision D5 | 2026-10-01: operator 2026-10-01: D5 answered, PyPI with TestPyPI staging (stage -> TestPyPI dev builds, main -> PyPI gated on tests; Trusted Publishing); tests run on a self-hosted runner luthen-observability maintains (W319, with fork-PR fences) | 2026-10-01: operator 2026-10-01: org name 'mikemol_tools' (D1, spelling pending: GitHub allows no underscore; both hyphen and hyphenless forms unclaimed); D2 answered: each repo keeps its git history (git filter-repo per subdirectory) | 2026-10-01: operator 2026-10-01: D3 answered, mtools stays as the workstream repo. 'Tooling repo' was unclear: it meant the shared build and check machinery every module uses; proposed homing it as its own module repo instead | 2026-10-01: operator 2026-10-01: D1 mikemol-tools; shared machinery as its own modules with atomization and composition (W321 decomposes it). All operator decisions answered | 2026-10-01: org created by the operator: mikemol-tools at 2026-10-01T12:04:59Z, verified via gh (free plan, 0 public repos, operator admin/active, default permission read, 2FA requirement OFF). No repo created yet: the first push is the icsstruct pilot after W318/W321 and the tooling atoms | 2026-10-01: all five shared-check atoms done (W323 9ab6a85 rules_py, W324 3ac8ac1 ruff, W325 372ec21 mypy, W326 c07542a mutants, W327 cd61477 ratchet) + W328 gate counts atoms. waypoints.title: Measure one representative module gate for the runner design: peak RSS, wall and CPU time, cold (first fetch) and warm, and whether bazel accepts --experimental_remote_downloader
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-01: measured bazel test //icsstruct/... in its own systemd user unit (cgroup accounting covers server + tests; 24-core host). COLD 1: 21.0 s wall, 121 s CPU, cgroup peak 8G (incl page cache; not split), IO read 145M / written 1.2G. COLD 2 (fresh output base + repository cache, sampled): 14.3 s, 66 s CPU, peak 2.71 GiB = anon 1.48 + file 1.09. waypoints.title: Package versions derive from the queue: a distribution's version is its stream's highest completed waypoint number
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-09: 2026-10-09 slice 1 (this tick): mikemol-paths-forward --delivered prints 0.0.<highest done W<n>> (0.0.0 when nothing is done), read-only, derived from the queue; the form 0.0.<n> chosen as monotone under PEP 440, a valid release segment and clearly pre-1.0. mtools prints 0.0.855 today. delivered.py + 4 tests + 4 warrants. Open for slice 2: a single queue gives every distribution the same number; per-distribution versions need a per-waypoint stream tag, which is a design choice not made here. | 2026-10-09: 2026-10-09 OPERATOR RULINGS (21:50Z): (1) the per-distribution stream problem is resolved by the planned split of mtools into one repo per package: each repo's own queue IS the stream, so mikemol-paths-forward --delivered (slice 1) is already the right number and no history derivation or per-waypoint tag is needed; slice 2 reduces to a dynamic version in each pyproject read from --delivered. (2) every content change has a waypoint behind it; the operator's rule makes that a monotone number. MY FINDING that sharpens it: the counter increments at MINTING, not completion, so a late-finished old card (minted before the last release) changes content without raising the highest completed number and would collide on PyPI (versions are immutable). Resolution, no .post suffix: a RELEASE GATE in mikemol-commit: a commit that changes a distribution's content must carry a waypoint numbered above the distribution's last RELEASED waypoint (recorded as a git tag v0.0.N), else refused with 'mint a new card for this change'. Then the version rises strictly with every content change by construction. Pre-split bridge (mtools single queue): not built; waits on the split's timing. Local +g<sha> versions on the sha-pinned wheels (PyPI rejects local versions) are replaced by this scheme. | 2026-10-09: 2026-10-09 OPERATOR RULING (21:55Z), SUPERSEDES the release-gate idea above: mint a NEW WAYPOINT FOR THE PUBLISH. A release mints 'publish <dist>' as a fresh card whose number is higher than everything minted before (the counter only increments); the build's version is 0.0.<that card's number>; the card is done when the upload succeeds. Strict increase holds by construction, independent of which older cards finish late; no commit-time check is needed. ORDER of the publish tool: mint, build with that version, upload, mark done; a failed upload leaves the card open as evidence and a retry mints a higher one (safe: PyPI only consumes a version on success). Per-package stream after the split is the repo's own queue. | 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 slice 2 pre-split bridge (the operator's 2026-10-09 ruling said it waits on the split's timing; built as a tool NOT used until greenlit): mikemol-wheel release-check ROOT SHA OUT --version 0.0.N stamps the version into the archived dists (versionstamp.py), committed pyprojects untouched. Slice 3 (the publish tool: mint card, build with its number, upload, mark done, tag) still open and needs the operator's upload go. Commit in flight. | 2026-10-15: Slices landed: 1 --delivered (earlier), 2 release-check --version 0.0.N (01935d2) and publish.yml requiring the version input (4208a06). Slice 3, the publish verb, is atomized into W1238 (enables W1143). The pre-split bridge is built but unused until the operator greenlights a release.

waypoints.title: Bound the bazel disk cache and output base on zram1: its real ceiling is compressed RAM, which compression ratio sets
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Incident 2026-10-06: zram1 (backs /tmp, /var/tmp, luthen scratch) hit its limit, ext4 failed on inode creation and remounted read-only; a reboot cleared it. df shows project-quota views (128G/32G/252G) of a device whose mem_limit is 48 GiB of compressed RAM and whose ratio was about 1.5:1 on bazel data, so it fills long before df says. waypoints.title: bazel admits each ACTION before it materializes data into zram, letting running actions finish and zram's LRU GC drain between them
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Operator 2026-10-06 (replaces the watchdog/stop-a-running-job design): the key is an admission check prior to the executor copying data into zram, catching actions as they are about to begin; existing actions continue; zram's own GC cycle drains it LRU-style, so waiting for it to fall is sound (not a permanent pin). Measured on this bazel (bazel help build --long): no built-in dynamic per-action gate, but three native pieces. (1) --local_extra_resources=zram_mb=N plus target tag resources:zram_mb:X makes bazel's own scheduler queue an action until the resource frees (static N per command: size it from zram headroom at command start minus a margin; only tagged targets take part, so tag them in dist_checks/gate_stages). (2) --run_under (tests) and --shell_executable (shell actions) run a wrapper before each such action: wait there on the LIVE zram reading, with membudget's zram gate (W837) as the waiter. (3) --sandbox_base picks where per-action sandbox trees go. Not yet shown: a hook that gates every local action type dynamically (compile/py actions run through the sandbox binary, not a shell). Next: prototype (2) for tests and (1) for the heavy macro targets on mtools, measure whether the heavy zram writers are covered, and only then decide whether the remainder needs remote execution (remote_executor is already configured). Still open from the earlier measurement: the staged-tree wrapper path and adoption in the other bazel repos.

waypoints.title: Python-file discovery is carried by corpus.py_files and pathwalk.expand: one should depend on the other
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Decide which of the five differences corpus keeps as policy and which it takes from pathwalk: the shape that fits is corpus.py_files = pathwalk.expand(operands, include_worktrees=..., exclude=<corpus's vocabulary as globs, bazel-* included>) plus corpus's root resolution; the open choices are (1) symlinked files, (2) the git requirement, (3) venv by marker rather than by name. Ask corpus's consumers (substrate imported it 173 times) before changing (1)-(3); until then keep both and record the decision here.
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-09: 2026-10-09 comparison by reading both (corpus.py_files versus pathwalk.expand), NOT equivalent in five ways: (1) corpus lists a symlinked .py file, pathwalk counts and refuses it; (2) corpus ignores registered worktrees, pathwalk skips them and REFUSES when git is absent (corpus is stdlib-only, no git); (3) corpus excludes a venv by the NAME .venv / site-packages, pathwalk by a pyvenv.cfg in the directory whatever its name; (4) corpus carries a default vocabulary (GENERATED_DIRS: build, dist, bazel-*, caches; _SKIP_PARTS), pathwalk has NO default list and prunes only what the caller names; (5) corpus resolves a relative request against the CWD first, then the root, and a file operand is returned as named. Policy versus mechanism: corpus is a policy (a vocabulary and a root resolution) and pathwalk the walk. corpus has no dependent in this repo. A collapse is therefore a behaviour decision for corpus's external consumers, not a mechanical swap.

waypoints.title: mikemol-sweep-budget sizes the mutation sweep from live headroom: its 0.4 of MemTotal default ignores swap pressure and the sandbox's own RAM (24 cells ran at once, 51482 MB, and filled swap)
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 OPERATOR PRINCIPLE (relayed by github-8f): true fixes are second-order, not first-order and not thresholds; rails are neither linear nor static. So the sweep budget is not sized once from MemTotal minus a constant: it is a LEASE that follows live headroom, level (MemAvailable plus swap and sandbox headroom), slope and acceleration, re-evaluated while the run goes, shrinking allowed parallelism when memory use accelerates and recovering when it decays. luthen W842 and host W26 supply the predictors. The vehicle should be the existing membudget and fence leases IF they can be resized mid-run (to be read from fence's source, not assumed). Publish rail engagement as a metric (leases granted, shrunk, refused): how often a rail engages is the oracle for throttling. The static nvme sandbox_base (host ~/.bazelrc, 2026-10-12) is the stopgap beneath it. | 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 READ (fence/src/mikemol/fence/membudget_cli.py:437 and admit.py): the ledger TOTAL can be resized in place under the lock keeping every live lease (membudget init --reset N, resize(): a sibling renamed over the ledger, so a reader sees old or new). A lease already held CANNOT be resized: admit.py has acquire, release and gc, no verb that changes a held lease's mb. So 'shrink while the run goes' has two real forms: (a) resize the total, which throttles NEW admissions only and leaves running cells at their size, or (b) a new fence verb to resize a held lease, which does not exist (a card of its own if the lease is to follow the live rail). Rail-engagement counts (granted, shrunk, refused) are not published today. | 2026-10-12: umbrella complete: rail model 210c7a7, railrun cc6ed56, railloop 4ea8988, mikemol-rail CLI 435fb26 [PUSHED]; paperkit letter written (W1035). waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 github-8f's suggested shape (a repo-level choice, theirs; to correct from the code): a resize verb for a HELD lease that does not kill or refuse; it changes the lease's size and, for a lease that owns a cgroup scope (W1026), sets that scope's memory.high to the new size, so the holder is throttled by reclaim pressure and not killed; a shrink below current use just applies pressure until the holder drops. Interim rail until it exists: resize the ledger TOTAL (membudget init --reset N) to throttle new admissions only. Read first: admit.py has acquire, release and gc and no verb that changes a held lease's mb; the ledger is rewritten as a sibling renamed over the file under the lock (Store.rewrite). | 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 github-8f measurement (linux-sources:W341, whole-session scope, 78 min, 6144 MB lease): memory.current peak 8521 MiB = anon 2901 + file 5566 + swap 5; the lease was 2.1x loose as anon, 39% over as current. RULING for this card: a lease means NON-RECLAIMABLE memory (anon + unreclaimable kernel: slab_unreclaimable, kernel stack, page tables), not memory.current; a lease resize moves that quantity.

waypoints.title: Design the waldo mode: a narrow tool holding one privilege, with a declared allowed set, refuse-with-diff, same-plan apply and witnesses
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 ask from luthen-observability:W889 (operator's word: a waldo is a narrow tool that holds one privilege and does only a declared action on behalf of others; the permission classifier fires on SHAPE, so the privileged act is a named verb with a declared contract). Two built instances to extract from: (1) luthen checks/apply_set.py + checks/apply_sets/<name>.json: plan fresh, compare with a declared allowed SUPERSET (+ required rows), refuse with a -/+ diff and apply NOTHING on any row outside it, else apply the SAME plan, then event-bound after-witnesses (exit code, json_empty, must_contain, must_match), one JSON verdict line; a converged row is absent so the set must be a superset; a finished oneshot unloads so the witness must be the journal. (2) amr-skills peer_token.py: bounded token, 0600 in a 0700 dir by atomic rename, prints only a fingerprint and expiry, refuses unless an identity is chosen, renews under a third of its life. Shared contract wanted: declared allowed set, refuse-with-diff, apply the same artifact, witnesses that cannot pass on defaults or a retry, fingerprint-only output, no secret in output. Read cassian-observability's six recipe files for the idiom before designing. NEXT: atomize (read the three sources, write .claude/design/W1053-waldo.md, then pure core / witnesses / CLI cards). waypoints.title: pycheck chooses the project's ruff config by ruff's own precedence and prints which config and line-length drove a refusal
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-13: 2026-10-13 RULING: a DEFECT (config discovery gap), not a house width. Read from the source: project_root.config_for returns the nearest pyproject.toml and pycheck_format.py passes it as ruff --config. When that pyproject has no [tool.ruff] table and a ruff.toml sits beside it (gcalculus), ruff gets the pyproject, finds no settings and formats at its default 88, while the repo's own ruff.toml says 100. Fix: choose the config by ruff's own precedence (.ruff.toml, then ruff.toml, then pyproject.toml WITH a [tool.ruff] table), and in every refusal print which config file drove the check and its line-length, so the answer is the repo's own and is visible. The mtools dists already all declare line-length = 100 in pyproject, so nothing changes for them. Do not add a fleet-wide width: a repo that declares one is obeyed. Test: a project with ruff.toml (100) and a pyproject without [tool.ruff] formats at 100 and names ruff.toml; a project with neither prints that it fell back to ruff's default. | 2026-10-13: 2026-10-13 REPRO (gcalculus:W262, via github-8f): the Edit gate refused a 7-line addition to cotype/harness/f_arm_floor.py (a PAPERKIT_CAPTURE_DIR spill of the witness's failure words) because the file is formatted at the repo's ruff.toml width 100 and the gate reformatted at 88, rewrapping three unrelated lines (e.g. an assert on (here / 'farm.py').is_file() with a parenthesised message). waypoints.title: mikemol-commit takes the repo-mutation lease for the whole commit, reset and push, and prints the repair when it cannot proceed
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-13: Symptoms (2026-10-13, attempt 13): post-commit printed [LOCAL: not on origin/main] with 'pre-push: BLOCKED, git operation in flight (index.lock present)' and 'PUSH ABANDONED (exit 1)'; afterwards git status showed the new files as staged deletions plus untracked (the real index never got the post-commit reset). Cause: an index.lock held at that moment (by another session's git, or by the commit's own steps; unknown which). Fix: retry the reset and the push a bounded number of times, name the holder if it can be told, and print the exact repair when it cannot. Related: W1040 (release the claim, remove a stale index.lock). | 2026-10-13: 2026-10-13 github-8f: likely cause (unverified, theirs): their 'katas.py tick end' started a background flush commit in 8 repos (mtools among them) at about the time of attempt 13, so it probably held the mtools index while the push and reset ran; I cannot confirm from here because the lock was gone by the time I looked (check the timestamps on the lock holder before accepting). Either way the fix is NOT a retry loop: commits collide on index.lock because nothing holds a mutex. Fleet rule (memory: repo mutations take a blocking lease): reuse the fence/membudget lease (total 1), wait on the holder's pid, never leave files staged. So: mikemol-commit takes the repo-mutation lease for the whole commit-reset-push, and the host's katas.py flush must take the SAME lease (recorded on W796, the kata graduation, so the kata calls the mode and not a second implementation). Print the repair command when it cannot proceed.

waypoints.title: katas flush skips repos with a live session and takes the repo-mutation lease for the others
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-13: 2026-10-13 github-8f: the host katas.py flush is a CONFIRMED FLAKE reported by two repos (mtools attempt 13 index.lock; el-openglo:W74 staged-directory gate refused: 'ln: ... .gate-outcomes.tsv: File exists'), therefore a blocker per the flakes rule. Root cause read from the sources: ~/github/.claude/katas/katas.py line 156 builds a raw 'git commit -m <msg> -- <paths>' argv and flush() (line 259) starts it with 'Queue: state sync' in every repo whose index.lock is absent AT THAT INSTANT (a check-then-act race, not a mutex), taking no repo lock and no isolated path. mtools' PORT (katas/src/mikemol/katas/fleet.py, W796/W875) already starts mikemol-commit via commits.commit_argv, but still guards only with in_flight() (index.lock exists) and the Fleet.skip_flush list. THIS CARD (smallest first): (a) skip any repo with a live session (they commit their own queue through mikemol-commit; only repos with no session need the sync), (b) take the repo-mutation lease (fence/membudget, total 1) for the rest, around the whole commit. Live-session detection is the open question: skip_flush is a caller-supplied list today; options are the session-claims registry (work_claims_hook) or the tick lock holder in the queue.

waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-13: 2026-10-13 github-8f/gcalculus:W263 + the 2026-10-12 memory incident. History: ~/.bazelrc had build --sandbox_base=/dev/shm; paperkit's gate ran 24 parallel sandboxes of ~2 GiB (48-51 GiB) in that RAM-backed tmpfs and put the host at the OOM brink, so github-8f moved the base to nvme (/var/cache/bazel-mikemol/sandbox). MEASURED today by gcalculus, same tree, one gate_root each: nvme base FAILED three times at 620-656 s, /dev/shm base PASSED at 275 s (outside any sandbox 258-271 s): the disk base multiplies some arm's CPU past a per-arm cap. A static path is wrong both ways. DESIGN: at launch, through the existing admit step (mikemol-bazel-admit and the membudget lease), the sandbox goes on a tmpfs only when MemAvailable minus the lease's projected footprint (jobs x measured sandbox size, from the gate ledger) stays above a reserve, and the JOB COUNT is lowered to fit rather than the sandbox moved; otherwise the nvme base, with the stretch it implies printed in the verdict. Measure the footprint per target in the ledger (instrument window written beside the cap, as window = cap / rate). The home rc then carries no sandbox_base. The host rc edit is the host's (github-8f), not done here. Interim: repos with a one-sandbox gate pass --sandbox_base=/dev/shm on their command line. Related: W1027 (peak sandbox-size check), W1024 (the rail), W1062 (shard timeout from solo runtime x stretch). | 2026-10-13: 2026-10-13 measured at /proc/loadavg 97/119/115 (24 cores): //pathsforward:test_cli solo, fresh execution each (--test_env=MEAS=...; --nocache_test_results is barred): default sandbox base critical path 3.91 s, elapsed 6.7 s; --sandbox_base=/dev/shm critical path 3.95 s, elapsed 6.4 s. No difference, and no stretch: solo it is ~4 s at full load. So the 60 s timeouts in the commit gate (attempt 23: test_cli, debtplan:test_mint timed out, test_store 138 s) are not sandbox-setup cost of one test and not CPU share of one test; they arise only when the gate runs ~840 targets at once (concurrency inside the gate). waypoints.title: katas flush ends a stuck gate by the hang witness; the wall-clock waiter --timeout and the gate-seconds ceiling are removed
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-13: 2026-10-13 operator rule 'Please avoid wall-clock timeouts' (2026-09-23/24; read at luthen-observability/checks/run_tool.py line 148-150, relayed by github-8f as fleet-wide, the repo-level reading being theirs). Reason: on a host loaded far past its core count, elapsed time measures contention, not whether work is stuck. Design: (1) CPU bound: the waiter sets RLIMIT_CPU on the child, always with RLIMIT_CORE=0; the limit is derived from the repo's last passing gate CPU seconds (from the child's rusage), not wall seconds. (2) Hang witness: the child is stuck when its log has not grown for a number of ITS OWN CPU-idle intervals; observe the log's size/mtime and the child's CPU time, and declare a hang only when CPU time has not advanced either (a loaded host starves wall time but not the ratio). (3) Keep ONE generous wall-clock backstop only if unavoidable, with a comment saying why. Replaces: waiter --timeout (W1105), fleet.ceiling's wall-clock seconds (W1106), LOG.seconds as wall seconds. Keep those working until this lands. | 2026-10-13: 2026-10-13 DESIGN CORRECTION: RLIMIT_CPU is per process, and mikemol-commit's real work runs in other processes (bazel), so an rlimit on the waiter's child bounds almost nothing. The compliant mechanism is the absence witness: W1125 streams the child's output into its log, W1124 reads the CPU of the child's whole process tree from /proc, W1126 declares a hang only when the log has stopped growing AND the tree CPU has stopped advancing, then ends the child. This card removes W1105's --timeout and W1106's wall-seconds ceiling once W1126 lands, keeping at most one generous commented backstop. | 2026-10-15: all children done: W1124, W1125, W1126, W1130 (derived by --close-umbrellas dry run, d0fba6a)

pathsforward --block-behind-open: block each ready card behind its open enablers (local and repo:W<n>), idempotent, dry run without --write
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-13: 2026-10-13 nemik:W476 (read in nemik's queue): ReadyBehindOpen (nemik:W465) flags a card stored ready or working while an open card enables it, for the case the umbrella rule (2+ own children) leaves out; fleet count 88, 55 of them paperkit W145-W200; mtools W1115-W1118 (behind W1122), W1019, W1100, W1128-W1130, W833. Design: a pure function over the State (blocked_on gets the open enablers, blocked_kind agent) in its own module, wired as an idempotent mode beside --prune-landed and --block-matching (W947 precedent: dry run without --write, then all-or-none). DECISIONS: (1) only READY cards are blocked; a WORKING card is being done by definition, so it is reported and left. (2) only OPEN enablers count (not done, not residue); a cross-repo enabler is read through the same foreign resolution as --prune-landed and written as repo:W<n>. (3) the existing prune returns the card to ready when the enabler lands, so no new unblock path. (4) The assumption to state in the output: it treats 'X enables Y' as 'Y waits for X'; an edge that is only a hint, not a prerequisite, should be dropped first (nemik's umbrella rule says the same). (5) a card that already has a blocked_on of its own keeps it and gains the enablers.

waypoints.title: mikemol-paths-forward mode that takes an operator ruling (the AskUserQuestion question and answer text, with its time) and lifts exactly the one held row it names, refusing every other change, so standing rule 5 holds against agents and not against the operator's own words

waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 DESIGN QUESTION before building (github-8f asked for W1194's distance): the mode takes ruling text from its caller and cannot verify the operator wrote it; an agent can type the same text, so a mode that lifts on recorded text moves rule 5's guard to whoever supplies the text. Options that hold against agents: (a) the operator runs the lift themselves in their own shell (the tool refuses when run by an agent session, by the env the harness sets); (b) the ruling is read from a file only the operator's side can write (a path outside the agent's write permission); (c) the lift needs a token the operator mints. Which is for the operator to choose; I have not picked one. Distance: not near until that is chosen; the code itself is one mode with a refuse-everything-else test. | 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 OPERATOR DECISION, relayed by github-8f (not verified by this session): the lift is authorised by the operator's TOTP from their phone; the code does not lift the row itself but authorises OpenBao to SIGN the ruling payload (card, ruling text, time) with a non-exportable transit key (luthen-observability:W1075, read: it currently describes a TOTP validate-only policy, so its text predates the signing step and luthen has to carry it). The lift mode: builds the canonical payload, submits it with the code for signing, records payload plus signature, and changes exactly the named held row only when the signature verifies against the transit public key checked into the repo. Tests: a valid signature lifts that row only; a signature over a different card or ruling text refuses; no signature refuses; wrong or reused code is OpenBao's to refuse. Split here: W1270 the pure core with an injected verifier (buildable now); W1271 how signatures are verified inside a dependency-free package (stdlib has no ed25519/ecdsa verify: options are an external openssl, a dependency, or opa); the OpenBao signing call is blocked on luthen-observability:W1075. | 2026-10-15: mtools half BUILT: lift core 20f7106 and the command line 078a057 (--lift JWS --jwk FILE). Left: luthen-observability:W1075 (the OpenBao transit key, its public JWK to check in, the signing request path); nudged them with the three concrete needs. Once the JWK exists, the repo checks it in and the operator runs the signing request, then --lift. | 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 luthen-observability-d9 (testimony): W1075 items 1-2 (transit ed25519 key exportable=false in terraform+Rego, public JWK from its public part, one-time raw-signature demonstration) are ready on luthen's side and do not wait on the operator; item 3, the request path, waits on the operator choosing (A) login MFA in front of a one-use sign-only token or (B) a broker. waypoints.title: Decide how the lift verifies an OpenBao transit signature without a new dependency in pathsforward
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 RULING (github-8f, repo-level): reuse opa, the dependency pathsforward pins. CHOSEN ROUTE: opa. RAN (not from memory): opa 1.20.2 from the bazel cache; 'opa capabilities --current' lists io.jwt.verify_eddsa (and es256/384/512, rs, ps, hs); a probe script (a scratch Python file using openssl genpkey ed25519 to make a key, a compact JWS with header alg EdDSA and canonical payload {card, ruling, time}, signed with openssl pkeyutl -sign -rawin, the public key as a JWK {kty OKP, crv Ed25519, x = base64url of the raw 32 bytes}) evaluated io.jwt.verify_eddsa(JWS, JWK): valid JWS -> true; the same signature over a payload naming a different card -> false; empty signature -> false; 64 zero bytes -> false. So the lift can verify with opa and no new dependency, and the openssl fallback is not needed. NOT PROVEN HERE: that OpenBao's transit ed25519 sign over the exact JWS signing input (non-prehashed) yields a raw signature this verifier accepts, and the form of the transit public key; that is luthen-observability:W1075's to demonstrate with a real key, and W1270's verifier seam should take the JWK so either way works.

waypoints.title: The commit hook enforces a plain commit body and a waypoint trailer, so the rule leaves the tick prompt

waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 MEASURED by running the tools on this queue. SHARED TOUCHES: (1) coordination is partly tool-covered: a status change takes a tag lease and refuses with 'cannot lease TAG: W<n> holds it' (lease.py, within one queue); cross-repo overlap is nemik-overlaps (nemik's). (2) --overlaps prints 22 tag groups here; 'hooks' alone lists 20 cards (W581 .. (3) What no tool does: tell the peer session; the rule 'coordinate with the peer' has no mechanism beyond reading the tag. TRIAGE AGAINST THE TREE: (4) --check (graph shapes) passes; --certify judges realizability; --unlinked reports 17 of 114 live cards unlinked (this tick's new cards among them). (5) --check-evidence is the closest 'is this true in the tree' tool and its answer DIFFERS from the truth on its own output: 15 findings on this queue, each a string that is not a file (a URL path /danger-api/echo, /adding-a-publisher, a fragment /bin/bash.002/min, an example /nonexistent.py, a placeholder /var/tmp/mikemol/gate/<repo>/tree), so it cannot be trusted as a triage gate. waypoints.title: pycodemod futureimport planner removes the annotations future import and quotes forward class names, listing unquotable bases
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-16: 2026-10-16 DESIGN from reading pycodemod's orempty (planner plan(text)->Planned wrapped by cli_typedargs.print_judged, judged by the project's mypy+ruff so a rewrite lands only when findings do not rise). The future-import verb is the same shape: a libcst planner that removes the import line. Mypy does NOT see the failure that matters (an unquoted forward reference is fine to mypy and a NameError on 3.13 at import), so the planner must itself quote three classes of annotation name: (1) a class used before its module-level definition or inside its own body, (2) a name bound only under 'if TYPE_CHECKING:' (346 of 453 tree modules have the TYPE_CHECKING import, so this is the dominant case), (3) a name from a module that would become a runtime import cycle. Class 2 interacts with W1343: Codon rejects TYPE_CHECKING itself, so a quoted TYPE_CHECKING-only name is an interim form; the end state turns those into real imports, where cycles then decide. Atomized: W1326a planner for classes 1 and 3-free case, dry run lists the sites; W1326b the TYPE_CHECKING-bound case; both before any --write. | 2026-10-16: commit 65ac1e5 (pushed): futureimport.plan, 4 tests. waypoints.title: The gate's bazel jobs count ignores that a mutants shard is itself a swarm of pytest processes
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-20: 2026-10-20 readings (github-8f's three checks): (1) With --local_cpu_resources=7 and hooks shards declaring cpu:8, eight shards (hooks 1, 6, 12, pycodemod 0, 1, pathsforward 5, treeio 0, debtplan 0) were ALL executing at once (pgrep of their runner shells): bazel neither waited for 8 free cores nor serialised them, so the cpu:K tag is not reserving anything for these sh_test shards. The pool cap alone does not stop the oversubscription; the 31 timeouts need another edge, e.g. --local_test_jobs sized as free cores divided by the declared K, or a host-ledger lease per shard. Reading the outcome when the run ends. (2) The gate runs mikemol-gate-jobs through the live bazel-bin link, so this edit changes every gate before it has passed one: the W1743 class (bazel-bin of a live working tree is not a pinned tool). Acceptable tonight; W1743 stays near the top. (3) The pool, like --jobs, is sampled once at gate start from load1, a spot reading; bazel's pool does not follow load during the run. | 2026-10-20: 2026-10-20 second reading (github-8f: why cpu:K did not reserve): the macro is NOT at fault. bazel query on //hooks:mutants_1 shows tags = [cpu:8], env MUTATE_JOBS=8 and MUTATE_SHARD=1/24, size = medium: the tag is on the sh_test. Bazel's own help documents --local_resources as limiting concurrent actions by test tags of the form resources:NAME:AMOUNT, and mentions cpu:3 only as the sandbox LIMIT form (--experimental_sandbox_enforce_resources_regexp). So cpu:8 is likely not the scheduling reservation; resources:cpu:8 may be. Eight-shard run with --local_cpu_resources=7: hooks 1 and 6, debtplan 0 and treeio 0 TIMED OUT (medium = 300 s); hooks 12, pycodemod 0 and 1, pathsforward 5 passed. To test: add resources:cpu:K beside cpu:K in the macro and rerun three hooks shards with a pool of 8, expecting one at a time. Caution (mine): a fence lease taken INSIDE the shard cannot work alone, because the wait counts against the test's own wall limit; the host-wide lease belongs around the gate's whole bazel invocation (the pool), with bazel's own tag reservation inside it. | 2026-10-20: landed 4a1f9869

waypoints.title: Mutants shards take their cores from a non-blocking fence/membudget ledger lease instead of sampling load1, so shards starting together divide the free cores (bounded by construction)
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-28: 2026-10-28 READ: the shards size their pool in check_mutants/mutate_runner.py pool_size(jobs, cpus, share, load1) via free_cores(cpus, load1) = max(1, round(cpus - load1)), with load_one() sampling the host load; shards that start together all read the same load and each take the same free cores. A grep of fence/src for a non-blocking, try-hold or no-wait lease mode finds none, so fence needs the primitive first. | 2026-10-28: 2026-10-28 READ fence/src/mikemol/fence: the ledger accounts MEMORY only (admit.Request carries mb; decide(request, ledger) is the pure admission, acquire blocks, so a try-acquire is decide plus _claim with no waiting), so cores are NOT a ledger resource today; but claims.py already has a NON-BLOCKING label claim (take(store, host, label, pid, epoch) returning an Outcome, drop, listing), which is the primitive this card needs: a core is a label claim. waypoints.title: Mutation runs are one bazel target per site in hierarchical BUILD files, so the cache skips every unchanged site

Conclusion matches github-8f's: the landing record is written on every call and every path, never behind a flag | 2026-10-25: 2026-10-25 nemik-84 ANSWERS (read from src/nemik/landings.py and hostroot's reader): (1) the reader takes a landing's time from the log record's _time and ignores any body field, so landed_at is kept ONLY if a stack emits its records together after the gate; (2) derive the stack, do not send its size: key plus index suffices (stack = records sharing a key; the reader infers a stack today from a run of equal gate_s, a guess); keep size only if refused or withdrawn entries must count in it; (3) only landed counts toward round size, refused and withdrawn are kept and counted apart as PRESSURE (a refused gate costs gate_s), never as throughput. TRAP A: the reader accepts event == 'landing' only, so the landed kind keeps the word 'landing' (refused and withdrawn get their own words, e.g. 'refused', 'withdrawn'). TRAP B: the reader is hostroot's flat-JSON reader (strings and lists of strings, no nested objects, no booleans): emit stack as flat keys stack_key and stack_index (and stack_size only if needed), pushed as the text true or false; cards as a list of strings is fine. FINAL SHAPE, flat for hostroot's reader (strings and lists of strings only): event = landing | refused | withdrawn (landed keeps the word 'landing'); repo; sha; subject; card (the primary, --waypoint); cards (list of every Waypoint trailer symbol); stack_key and stack_index (strings, absent for a direct landing); path = direct | stack | train; gate_s; verdict = pass | refused | withdrawn; reason (refused and withdrawn only); pushed = 'true' | 'false'; notes (list of 'key=value' strings the declared pre-steps print on lines beginning NOTE, so host_rows rides as 'host_rows=2' with no luthen-specific field in mikemol-commit) | 2026-10-25: 2026-10-25 CORRECTION OF MY OWN EARLIER FINDING, from reading both writers. I said the single-commit path writes no landing record unless --ship is passed. WRONG IN ONE WAY THAT MATTERS: there are two different writers. (a) --ship goes through verdictlog.ship_text then ship_events, which spools the run's VERDICT events (event_of and gate_event_of lines, their own shape) for a detached drainer; (b) the 'landing' record nemik reads (event landing, repo, sha, card, gate_s, pushed, verdict) is made ONLY by commit_span.landing_records and shipped by commit_span.emit_landings, whose single caller in the package is emit_stack (commit_span.py line 373), the STACK path. So a single commit never writes a landing record, with or without --ship, and luthen's W1636 (adding --ship to checks/land.py) will NOT make nemik see its landings. The fix is the card itself: one landing record written by every path

waypoints.title: Read stackrun.gate_tip and gatephase: where does each check's captured output live when a stack is REFUSED, and can the last 40 lines of the failing check follow the REFUSED line
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-25: 2026-10-25 instance (luthen-observability-ab): luthen W1645's one-entry stack refused ~19:55Z 'a check measured a defect ... culprit: unattributed', identical content landed on resubmit as 896e3a0f; luthen kept 400 characters and mtools' ledger kept nothing readable: luthen/.git/mtools holds no stack file from that window (stackfreeze.forget unlinks items.json at the end of a run; .snap and .trees are replaced). Second instance for W1662/W1996/W2007. | 2026-10-29: 2026-10-29 READ stackrun.py run (lines 225-300) and measured on today's refusals. ANSWER: a refused stack's captured output is NOT stored by mtools: gate_tip returns a CompletedProcess whose stdout+stderr are written whole to the client's stdout (out.write(shown)) BEFORE the REFUSED line, then _judged adds its note, then 'REFUSED ... culprit_note'. So the failing check's section ('--- <check>' and its tail, ending with 'reproduce only the refusing rung: bazel test //x:y') already PRECEDES the REFUSED line in the client's output, as seen in today's hooks-c and pathsforward-b refusals. What is lost is only what the CALLER keeps: luthen kept 400 characters, and stackfreeze.forget removes items.json at the end of a run, so nothing on disk survives a refusal. The fix is therefore not a new capture but (a) a copy of the output to a file beside the stack file that survives the run (W2153's tombstone is the natural place: key, rc, failing check, culprit, first 40 lines of the failing section) and (b) callers reading to the end of the client output, not the first 400 characters. Both are carried by W2153; this card is the answered question.

waypoints.title: BuildBuddy's BES endpoint accepts connections again after the 2026-10-29 reboot, so a submit's presubmit can upload its BEP
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-29: 2026-10-29 from source (github-42 asked why luthen's checks.land landed 85603ff1 with BES down while mtools' presubmit refused W2067 at rc 34): both repos land through mikemol-commit, so the commit path is the same; the DIFFERENCE IS EACH REPO'S BAZEL CONFIG. mtools .bazelrc lines 180-183 set, for every build, --remote_cache=grpc://buildbuddy-bes...:1985, --remote_cache_async=true, --bes_backend=grpc://buildbuddy-bes...:1985 and --bes_results_url. luthen's .bazelrc sets --bes_backend only under build:remote (line 19) and build:incluster (line 25), so luthen's default build never contacts the endpoint. The two failures seen here: (1) 'Failed to query remote execution capabilities: finishConnect failed: Connection refused' fails the test action (the remote cache capability query), (2) 'The Build Event Protocol upload failed: All 4 retry attempts failed' makes bazel exit 34 on a passing build. NOT VERIFIED: whether a bes_upload_mode other than the default would stop (2) from failing the build, and whether a remote-cache outage can fall back to local execution. Either needs a .bazelrc change, which only the operator may make (standing rule 1), so this is an operator decision: treat BEP upload and remote cache as best-effort telemetry in mtools, as luthen's default effectively does. | 2026-10-29: 2026-10-29 FIX BUILT, verified locally: bazel_admit.degrade (service_address reads the endpoint from the workspace .bazelrc, can_connect probes it, OFF_FLAGS --remote_cache= --bes_backend= --bes_results_url= inserted right after the verb when it refuses; nothing changes when it accepts). No .bazelrc edit, so no operator cosign was needed. Verified by running, not recall: --remote_local_fallback does NOT help (it covers remote execution; the cache capability query still fails the action); --bes_upload_mode=fully_async removes the BEP exit 34 but not the cache failure; --remote_cache= with BES off passes. A plain bazel test with no flags now exits 0 while port 1985 refuses connections (the admit note prints). Eight targets pass in one run: hooks test_after_compaction, test_bin_launchers_argv, test_commit_withdraw, test_bazel_admit (18), ratchet test_declaration, pathsforward test_blocked_on_blank, test_regressions, test_retros, transcriptstruct test_commitments. waypoints.title: The observed-type annotator tells Literal[False] from bool for an exit that only ever returned False, by keeping values and not only types
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-06T14:39:20Z: 2026-11-06: taken at the Stop hook's ask while W2219 batch 33 holds the gate; no code for this card this turn. | 2026-11-08T16:25:23Z: 2026-11-08: DECIDED (read observed._builtin_spelling and annotating._EXITS first). The observer keeps types, not values, and annotating.py line 150 already sends an observed bool return of __exit__ to the worklist as a candidate, never an annotation. DECISION: leave it to the worklist for good; do NOT extend the observer to record value sets. Reason: a finite set of runs that saw only False cannot establish that True is unreachable, so Literal[False] is not observable from runs (the realizability observable gate), and the value-set would change the observer's contract for every site. The claim IS provable from the code: when every return in the exit is a False literal. That is a body rule, carded as W2372 (annotating/narrowing, not observer). el-openglo's selftest-only case stays theirs, and still gets the candidate line. No code changed; the closing evidence is this reading.

waypoints.title: A pure module created_record appends the paths a session's Write tool made to a per-session record beside the transcript, and answers whether a path is one the session created, including any path under the session's own scratchpad directory
waypoints.next_bounded_step: DESIGN (W1919's open decision): the record lives beside the transcript, <transcript dir>/created/<session_id>.jsonl, the same durable place as W2117's compaction records (a scratch area is lost with a reboot). One JSON line per Write: {path (absolute, resolved), at}. API: record(transcript, session, path, now) appends one line, never raises; created(transcript, session) reads the set of paths; is_created(path, paths, scratchpad) is True when the path equals or lies under a created path or under the scratchpad directory (the session's own scratch area counts as created whole, since the harness hands it out empty). A path outside the transcript's project is still recordable. Tests: append then read; a child of a created directory counts; a path outside does not; the scratchpad root counts; an unreadable record reads as empty and says so, never as 'everything created'. waypoints.title: Post-land sync leaves stale pre-landing bytes in main's tree after a --freeze-from stack; sync every path or report the skipped
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02: taken; reading the post-land sync in the hooks stack landing code first. | 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02 peer evidence (luthen-observability, W1880): landings 72e69363 (8 paths, host/files.json stale), 1b3d7e49 (6, dr_params_test.py), 4c3fed81 (checks/gate.py, still stale), d47bc0b8 (7, record_types_test.py and record_types.json; second submit of its card), 3143cfcd (5, exposition_baseline.json). Common: another stack queued behind, or a host apply pass running; clean landings had neither. Each stale diff is the exact inverse of the landed commit. The stack files are gone (built in a temp dir). The live stale state is inspectable in the peer tree for 4c3fed81. | 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02 READ: the sync is isolated.refresh_tree(root, paths, start, run), called by stacklanding.land right after update-ref and refresh_index (W2193). Per path: diff --quiet HEAD equal -> skip; diff --quiet start equal -> restore --source=HEAD --worktree; else named as 'working copy differs from HEAD and was left'. So it already reports skipped paths, in the land output's notes. Candidate causes of the peer's stale files, none confirmed: (1) a queued second stack or a host apply pass writes the pre-landing bytes back AFTER refresh_tree ran (a race no per-path judgement can see; needs a final verify pass); (2) start is the previous stack's tip, so a copy at the earlier bytes equals neither HEAD nor start and is named 'differ', which the peer may not have seen; (3) a diff --quiet that fails with rc above 1 (an index.lock) is read as 'differs from start' and also lands in differ, never as an error. Nothing edited. | 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02 peer reply and a read-only look at their live case: gate.py in luthen-observability has HEAD holding check_record_types (2 hits) and the working file holding none; the index equals HEAD (diff --cached empty); diff --name-only HEAD lists it. So it is a worktree-only staleness at exactly the start commit's bytes, the branch refresh_tree should restore. waypoints.title: Version contract step 2: each distribution declares its own semver and the ranges it accepts from its siblings
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Waits on W2233; when it lands, do: Version contract step 2: each distribution declares its own semver and the ranges it accepts from its siblings
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02 operator refinement (see W2236 for the verbatim words): each component carries its own semver with the sha as BUILD METADATA, x.y.z+sha, and x, y, z do not change when nothing that decides them changed, even if the sha did. The operator is unsure which check decides the bump and says so. THE HOST'S READING (github:W93), offered as input, NOT a ruling: the INTENSIONAL check diffs each component's declared surface (public API signatures, CLI argparse, the state schemas it reads and writes): removed or changed is x, added is y, an identical surface is z; the EXTENSIONAL check runs the prior release's tests against the new code, and a failure forces x. Common pattern: the intensional diff PROPOSES and the extensional run VERIFIES. THE DESIGN THAT GOES BACK MUST STATE THE BUMP RULE, and must answer what counts as a component's surface (and whether a pyproject's declared console scripts and a state file's format version are part of it). | 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02 operator ruling via github-33 (github:W94), verbatim, replying to the host's note that the intensional check 'trusts the declaration to be complete': 'we cannot decouple without that. But this is why our mutators.regex (and possibly any other mutation testing we're doing) is so helpful; it minimizes, structuralizes and contextualizes that scope and risk.' RULING: the bump decision rests on the DECLARED SURFACE, and mutation testing bounds the risk that the declaration is incomplete. HOST'S READING for the design: a mutant that SURVIVES inside a component's declared surface marks where the declaration is not backed by tests, so a surface-diff bump could miss a break exactly there. THE DESIGN MUST STATE how mutation results bear on the bump, for example surviving mutants on the declared surface are reported with the bump, or block a z-only bump on that component; the bump rule goes back with that coupling as part of the W2233/W2234 design. | 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02 operator CORRECTION via github-33 (github:W94), verbatim: 'That's not just a standing for behavioral checking, that's behavioral checking as driving the test declarations.' So: behavioral checking DRIVES the declarations, it does not stand in for them. A surviving mutant on a component's declared surface is the TRIGGER to mint the missing test and so EXTEND the declaration; the earlier host suggestion (report survivors, or block a z-only bump) is WITHDRAWN. The surface declaration is the OUTPUT of mutation and its completeness is CHECKED by mutation, not trusted. The design must state the loop: surviving mutant on the surface -> a test is minted -> the declaration grows -> the bump rule reads the grown declaration. | 2026-11-09T09:33:22Z: 2026-11-08: step 2 follows step 1 (W2233, the format-version handshake) in the version contract, and the whole design waits behind the operator's ranking of it below ratchet paydown (W2232). The design must also state the bump rule with the mutation loop (surviving mutant on the surface, test minted, declaration grows).

waypoints.title: Version contract step 3: the gate records the resolved versions it ran with, so a range stays reproducible
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Waits on W2234; when it lands, do: Version contract step 3: the gate records the resolved versions it ran with, so a range stays reproducible
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02 operator addition via github-33 (github:W94), verbatim: ''even if the sha does' ... Meanwhile, the version gets a convenient provenance indicator.' CONSEQUENCE for this card: the +sha suffix doubles as a PROVENANCE marker, so a gate that records its resolved versions as x.y.z+sha already holds the exact commit it ran, with no lookup; the same holds for luthen's user_tools receipts. The design carries this: the gate's recorded line is the resolved x.y.z+sha per component, and a reader recovers the commit from the suffix alone. | 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02 operator addition via github-33, verbatim: 'this is where topology and hott tie in. You're touching on covering n+1-paths over n-paths.' HOST'S READING, offered for the design and NOT as a formal claim: each x.y.z+sha is a POINT; a sha move at fixed x.y.z is a PATH asserting the two builds are equivalent on the surface; the gate's record of resolved versions with its verdict is the EVIDENCE covering that path; and mutation-driven tests cover that evidence. Each level needs a cover one level up. THE DESIGN MUST SAY WHAT WITNESSES EACH LEVEL: point (a version line with its sha), path (the record that two shas share x.y.z and the surface is equal), evidence (the gate verdict tied to the resolved versions), and the cover of that evidence (the mutation-driven tests and their survivor count). | 2026-11-09T10:04:08Z: 2026-11-08: step 3 follows steps 1 and 2 of the version contract (W2233, W2234), and the whole design waits behind the operator's ranking of it below ratchet paydown (W2232). The design must name the witness at each level: point, path, evidence, and the cover of that evidence.

waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02 READ across the remaining subprocess paydown (all plain-capture entries are now converted): the entries left that a one-shot capture cannot take need a LIVE HANDLE: fence tests/test_watcher.py (a real Popen and a signal), mutantcell tests/test_eval.py (Popen of a sleeper and a process-group kill), pathsforward tests/test_store.py and tests/test_lock.py (real racing processes), webpage tests/test_browser.py (_poker holds a Popen[bytes] across a probe), buildtel proc.stream (os.pipe stderr and Popen) and its tests/test_proc.py. A typed Child in procrun.proc (the one module with the exemption) would wrap Popen: pid, poll, wait(timeout), terminate, kill, send_signal, and an iterator over stderr lines, so a consumer names no subprocess type. CONSTRAINT FOUND: a dist that other repos VENDOR as a wheel (transcriptstruct, atomicwrite, frontier, icsstruct, rulerseq, cvdcore, ratchet, corpus, waldo, fence, hooks, pathsforward) cannot gain a RUNTIME procrun dependency without those consumers vendoring procrun too; the five runtime edges added so far (ledger, gradekit, scan, memres, pytestspec) were checked: no repo under ~/github vendors or path-sources them. Check this before every runtime procrun edge. Design the Child API as a card note first. | 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02 DESIGN (from reading the consumers): procrun.proc gains spawn(argv, cwd=None, env=None, stdin='inherit', output='inherit') -> Child, with stdin and output each Literal['inherit','discard'] (no booleans: the FBT rules). Child is a small class over the Popen it owns, in the one exempt module: pid (int property), poll() -> int | None, wait(timeout: float | None = None) -> int (raising the exported TimeoutExpired), kill(), terminate(), send_signal(sig: int), and the context-manager protocol (kill and wait on exit so a test never leaks a process). WHAT EACH CONSUMER NEEDS, measured: fence test_watcher: spawn a shell with stdin discarded, command.pid, command.wait(timeout); pathsforward test_store and test_lock: spawn with env and both output streams discarded, wait(timeout=...) (and expects TimeoutExpired for a blocked locker), poll() in a loop; webpage test_browser: spawn, kill(), wait() and an annotation for _poker's return (Child, not Popen[bytes]); mutantcell test_eval: spawn a sleeper, child.pid, and cell_eval.kill_tree(child), whose parameter is typed Popen in src/eval.py (exempt by its own entry), so kill_tree must take a Child (or a Protocol with pid and kill/wait) and its other caller must not break; buildtel proc.stream: stderr lines while it runs, which needs an iterator over the child's stderr, a second method (stderr_lines()) or a callback parameter on spawn; buildtel is the heaviest, take it last. NOT IN SCOPE: capturing output of a live child (none of the six needs it except buildtel's stderr). Constraints: dists that other repos VENDOR cannot gain a runtime procrun edge (see earlier note); these six are not vendored (fence is: check, fence keeps procrun dev-only, which fits since only test_watcher needs it). | 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02 CONSTRAINT CONFIRMED with a case: amr-skills VENDORS the mikemol_mdstruct and mikemol_pathwalk wheels (amr-skills/pyproject.toml lines 55 and 58), so pathwalk/src/.../walk.py's git call cannot move to procrun.capture without giving pathwalk, and so mdstruct, a RUNTIME procrun dependency, which breaks amr-skills' lock unless it vendors procrun too. pathwalk and mdstruct therefore keep procrun dev-only, and walk.py's per-responsibility entry stays unless amr-skills vendors procrun (ask them via the revendor list: procrun is on it now, W2230). waypoints.title: Adopt luthen's ready_wake as a standard loop tool: a writer mode or a sibling mikemol-ready-wake that prints one line per change
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Build mikemol-ready-wake in pathsforward per the design in evidence, after paydown; draft the loop-prompt line for operator sign-off (change-review) and do not edit the prompt.
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-03: 2026-11-02 PROPOSAL from luthen-observability (their W1931; operator ask 2026-11-02: 'get mtools and/or nemik to adopt ready_wake, so the tool is part of the standard set'): adopt checks/ready_wake.py (landed there as 54823aa8, 9 tests in ready_wake_test.py) as a standard loop tool. A monitor-grade event source: run as a Monitor it prints ONE line when something changes and is otherwise silent ('ready cards 264 -> 263' for the count of ready cards in the queue, or '<repo>:W<n> working -> done' for the status of any peer card one of THIS queue's BLOCKED cards cites, read from that peer's own queue under the fleet root). CONTRACT TO KEEP: the first snapshot is silent; an unreadable peer queue or card reads 'unreadable', never 'done'; a queue caught mid-write is skipped, not a change; an unreadable own queue exits 7; --once prints the snapshot as JSON; --poll N seconds. Reads the same queue file and the same blocked_on citations the writer owns, so the writer's schema is its only dependency. The operator's rule (2026-11-02, work-driven loop): the loop works while cards are ready, stops when none are, and is WOKEN by events, not a clock; the cron is a backstop. SUGGESTED HOME: a writer mode (--watch) or a sibling mikemol-ready-wake, plus ONE LINE IN THE LOOP PROMPT ('arm it as a Monitor, 30 min cap, re-arm on expiry; the cron is a long backstop'). The loop prompt line changes only with the operator's sign-off (change-review skill): do NOT edit it from a peer's proposal. OPEN: self-caused noise (a session's own status updates move the ready count; suppressing it needs the writer's holder id). The CONDITION half (apply refused/applied, a file appearing, a stamp moving) is nemik's witnesses (nemik:W58, W1513/W1514), asked separately. RANK: below ratchet paydown (operator 2026-11-02). | 2026-11-03: 2026-11-02 READ ready_wake.py at 54823aa8 (170 lines, stdlib plus checks.jsonio). FINDINGS FOR THE DESIGN: (1) It parses the queue JSON itself, which the writer's rule forbids for other readers (the writer is the one reader and writer of the state file); the writer already has read modes (--ready-count, --hash, --queue, --payload, --show), so an adopted version should call them, not open the file. (2) Its ready count is the RAW status=='ready' count, which is not the workable count: the writer's --ready-count says 115 now, and tick-open's 'ready N' line uses the workable rule (ready_cards in closegate.py excludes cards behind an open enabler). A wake on the raw count would fire on moves that change no workable card. (3) SELF-CAUSED SUPPRESSION via the tick lock's holder WILL NOT WORK as proposed: --update, --add and --ledger do not take the lock (the lock is the tick's, taken by --tick-open), so a session's own status updates happen with no holder recorded. What does exist: the writer's state hash (--hash, v2:...) changes on every write, and the ledger lines carry session=<id>. A suppression design: the monitor compares the hash it sees with the hash the session recorded after its own last write, or the writer exposes 'last writer session' in the state; this needs a writer change. (4) A peer card's status is read from the peer's queue file directly (same objection as 1; the right call is nemik's reader, nemik-inbound/--show on the peer path, or the writer pointed at the peer's state with --show). (5) The contract in the docstring is sound and worth keeping: silent first snapshot, unreadable never done, mid-write skipped, exit 7. (6) Monitor use is compatible: stdout lines, flush after each batch, an exit on an unreadable queue. NEXT STEP when paydown allows: write the design (sibling mikemol-ready-wake in pathsforward, built on --ready-count and --show, with the self-caused question settled), and draft the loop-prompt line for the operator. | 2026-11-03: 2026-11-02 luthen-observability agrees with all four findings. Their note: in their repo the raw and workable counts are equal today (261 and 261), so their local copy behaves the same; the difference shows only behind an open enabler (as in mtools). Self-caused suppression by hash-compare needs the monitor to be told the hashes the session recorded after its own writes (a file the session appends to, or a writer-exposed last-writer record): the design choice is mine. Their card is blocked on mtools:W2247. | 2026-11-09T11:46:41Z: 2026-11-08 DESIGN (no code): HOME is a sibling console script mikemol-ready-wake in the pathsforward dist, not a writer mode, because it is a long-running poller and the writer is a one-shot verb. READS only through the writer's verbs, never the state file: workable ready count from --ready-count (not the raw status count), a peer card from the writer pointed at the peer's state with --show (the reader stays the one owner of the schema). CONTRACT KEPT from ready_wake.py: first snapshot silent; unreadable reads 'unreadable', never 'done'; a queue caught mid-write is skipped; an unreadable own queue exits 7; --once prints the snapshot as JSON; --poll N seconds. SELF-CAUSED SUPPRESSION (the open question): the session appends the state hash the writer prints after each of its own writes to a small file it names with --own FILE (the writer already prints state_hash=v2:... after every update); the monitor stays silent when the hash it sees is one listed there and the counts it reports are unchanged from the last print. A writer change (last-writer session in the state) is the alternative and is rejected here because it changes the state schema for one reader. LOOP PROMPT: one line, drafted by me, edited only with the operator's sign-off. FALSE-POSITIVE COST: a hash not in --own (a peer's write) wakes the session, which is the point. Not built; below ratchet paydown (operator 2026-11-02). | 2026-11-26T03:17:18Z: 2026-11-26: the card's own rule is 'below ratchet paydown' (operator 2026-11-02), and the paydown ledger is W2887 (the 55 owed ratchet keys classified); the design (sibling mikemol-ready-wake on --ready-count and --show, --own hash file for self-caused suppression) stands unbuilt. Note for the design: the pinned mikemol-watchdog now wakes a session on QUIET (exit 8), not on a peer card's status change, so this card's peer-event half is still not covered by it.

waypoints.title: Ratchet counts a house-config per-responsibility relief (tests/test_*.py = S101) as an owed key that has no fall: decide whether pace excludes or only counts growth
blocked_on: operator: decide whether the pace guard owes a fall on a house-config per-responsibility relief (tests/* = assert): (a) exclude declared house-config reliefs from the owed list, (b) count them only on growth, or (c) keep counting them and treat hooks paydown as the standing tax on every stack
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Write the ruling options for the operator with this measurement attached: (a) exclude declared house-config reliefs from the owed list, (b) count them only on growth, (c) keep, and name hooks paydown as the standing tax on every stack.
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-03T19:03:29Z: 2026-11-03 MEASURED from a real refusal (W1956 submitted alone, after icsstruct landed): the pace guard lists about 37 owed pyproject files; 34 of them read 'required fall 1 (a few 2 to 9), observed 0, paydown cards: none named', and the dists I could inspect (grade, htmlstruct, katas, endpoints, ratchet apart from its two subprocess entries) carry only the tests/* assert relief or a runtime subprocess entry in a vendored dist, which no stack can lower cheaply. Only hooks (required 72, observed 28, cards W2219 W2220 W2221) and gatecheck (4, W2212) have named paydown cards. So the guard demands a paydown that, for most dists, does not exist, and every stack must therefore carry a hooks (or similar) conversion to be admitted. This is the W2255 question in its measured form: whether per-responsibility reliefs count as owed at all. Not mine to change (standing 2), recorded for the operator. | 2026-11-09T12:21:13Z: 2026-11-08 OPTIONS FOR THE OPERATOR, with the 2026-11-03 measurement (34 of about 37 owed pyproject files read 'required fall 1, observed 0, paydown cards: none named'; only hooks and gatecheck have named paydown cards): (a) EXCLUDE declared house-config reliefs from the owed list: a dist whose only entry is tests/* assert owes nothing; stacks stop needing a hooks conversion for those dists; cost: a real relief that should fall is invisible to the pace, so declaring one becomes a way out. (b) COUNT ONLY ON GROWTH: the relief is baselined and refused when it grows, never owed a fall; cost: none of paydown's rate pressure on it, but the ratchet still holds the line. (c) KEEP: every stack carries a hooks (or similar) conversion, W2219 stays the standing tax, and the 34 dists whose relief cannot fall cheaply stay owed forever. My recommendation is (b): it keeps the no-growth guarantee and drops the demand that cannot be met. Evidence I did this week: ratchet's own per-file entries went 6 to 1 by moving subprocess onto procrun, leaving only the tests/* assert, which is exactly the shape that has no fall.

A parked repo reads PRESENT with verdict dormant, so the bare series is live for every repo and cannot be the companion unfiltered; ok means the repo's ledger moved in 60 min (any line kind), not strictly that a tick hook ran. The fit is the series filtered to verdict ok or stale. The registry field takes a plain dotted name (the emitter stores a string), so the answer back is to ask luthen-observability to mint luthen.claude.loop.armed{repo} (1 for ok or stale, absent otherwise), a continuous series they own; W2260 then names it as freshness_companion, owner mtools, and does NOT emit with a near-miss companion. Publisher cadence asked. | 2026-11-26T03:34:57Z: 2026-11-26 luthen-observability CARDED luthen-observability:W3032 (enables this card): emit luthen.claude.loop.armed{repo}, value 1 while the repo's verdict is ok or stale, ABSENT for dormant, disarmed, future and unknown, a continuous metric luthen owns, pushed by the publisher beside luthen.claude.loop.liveness; freshness_companion string once shipped: luthen.claude.loop.armed (family prefix luthen_claude_ already has a registry row, freshness generated). waypoints.title: Per-object diamond targets: each dist gets precondition, build, test and coverage targets, and a dependent's precondition depends on its dependency's coverage
waypoints.next_bounded_step: FIRST MECHANISM PROVEN by W2718 (done): an AST-normalized copy of a dependency cuts off a dependent's unit tests on a comment-or-whitespace edit (memres on procrun: 29 re-runs became 16, all 13 unit tests cut off; BES 148ec565-6671-48d8-a49f-d5f575cffc1e vs f9dafff3-d164-4559-b1ad-63cbf5eae62c). NEXT, in order: (1) point the 12 mutation shards and :.venv at the normalized copy too (the grid mutates memres, not procrun) and re-measure, expect 16 to fall toward 4; (2) a signatures-only artifact (a .pyi from the parse tree) for mypy, the interface digest proper; (3) the rule as a dist macro with a per-edge switch (constraint 3); (4) combine with W2717's per-module libraries. waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-03T13:14:40Z: 2026-11-03 operator, key point: test results are build artifacts consumed downstream; coverage validates the test evidence carried along the edge as a build input, so verifying an object is a prerequisite to consuming it (assurance edges: Y_p depends on X_c; transitive via Y_c, not by naming X). DESIGN CONSTRAINTS read from that: (1) a build target depending on a *_test target gets the executable, not a run: X_t must be a rule whose action runs the test and writes a result file (verdict, failing names) that X_c declares as an input; (2) X_c's output must be content-stable: only what X's inputs determine (declared-surface hash, verdict, coverage figures, dependencies' assurance digests), NEVER a source revision, execution id, time or path, or every commit changes it and early cutoff is lost (the sha stays build metadata per the one-sha-release ruling); (3) a cached pass is only meaningful if the test action is deterministic given its declared inputs, so tests that read the host, run git or race processes must be made hermetic first (the procrun and spawn conversions and off-host sdist work serve this); (4) whether X_t consumes X_b is declared per object, not imposed; (5) more verifiers (ruff, mypy, pycheck, mutation, warrant pairing) join the same fan-in into X_c, replacing checks that run outside bazel; (6) coverage is evidence, not a correctness certificate: X_c is an assurance aggregation boundary. | 2026-11-03T13:42:22Z: 2026-11-03 first reading from W2261: a comment-only change in procrun (a leaf) re-ran 37 of 45 targets across procrun and memres, because memres is one py_library with one dependency list for all its tests (the graph has a path from test_mem_db to //procrun:procrun though only railcli.py imports it). This is the case the diamond fixes: with procrun_c as a content-stable digest of its declared surface and verdicts, and memres's precondition depending only on that digest, the comment change leaves the digest byte-identical and nothing in memres re-runs. It also shows the first thing to fix inside a dist: tests need per-module cones, not one library per dist. | 2026-11-09T14:14:11Z: 2026-11-08: the design note is written at .claude/design/W2262-diamond-targets.md (uncommitted): the four targets per dist, five invariants each with the failure it prevents, the success test (procrun_c byte-identical across a comment-only change), and what is unknown. waypoints.title: Answer: should the round check admit a working mark for a card being built, refusing only what is submitted outside the round
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-06T21:42:20Z: 2026-11-06 ANSWER (nemik:W2027; read hooks round_check.py, its docstring and composition()): (1) THE RULE REFUSES ONLY ON TWO FACTS TOGETHER: a ready round card is not in the working set AND a working card is outside the round (composition: outside = working minus round; skipped = ready round cards not working; empty if either is empty). A working mark on a ROUND card is never refused, with or without other marks. (2) WHAT IT DISCOURAGES: any working mark on a card OUTSIDE the round, including a card truly being built (a peer ask, an enabling card, a card minted this hour), unless EVERY ready round card is already working. That is the rational-zero state: the only way to hold one honest outside mark without a refusal is to mark the whole ready round, so sessions mark nothing. (3) THE FIX, which admits the mark: composition() gains a 'building' set and subtracts it from outside. A card is BEING BUILT when a live stack or a held scratch tree names it: the gate's in-flight and queued waypoints (mikemol-commit --in-gate) plus the scratch registry; the writer already has this notion for the opposite case (--working-stale, W2195: working cards no live stack names). Then the refusal is exactly what the operator wants: a ready round card passed over for a working card that nothing is building (an empty mark) or a STACK SUBMITTED outside the round. The submit-side refusal needs no set at all: the stack's own waypoints are what is being built. (4) WHY MY QUEUE HOLDS MARKS AND THE OTHERS DO NOT: honestly, mostly because of me: the tick-stop hook ('ready work and no card moved this turn: take W.. and advance it') told me to mark a named card working every turn and I did, about 85 times, with no work behind most of them; the round check never fired on them because no ready round card was skipped until W2200 entered the round this hour, when it fired at once. waypoints.title: A withdraw request that cannot stop a stack refuses at request time with too late, will land, and an accepted one holds
waypoints.next_bounded_step: After b66: read commit_withdraw._ask_to_stop and .githooks/pre-commit phase() (line 148), design the atomic claim with a happens-before argument, build the forced-interleaving witness (pause landing between claim and apply, and between the last phase and the claim).
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-08T00:06:52Z: 2026-11-07 github-14: luthen requested withdrawal of an in-flight stack about 23:45Z and it LANDED anyway as 0ed0fe0b, carrying a file the session had already deleted from its worktree, because the freeze was taken at submit; 561bb7e4 landed after withdrawal too (second time). Required: a withdraw that cannot stop the stack must refuse at request time and say too late, will land (W2142 asks the same wording); one that is accepted must hold. TO NAME: where the request is read relative to landing, and the race. PINNED PATH (answered to github-14): luthen-tools live/nemik is the nemik install at eb3fd9c8 whose mikemol_hooks dist-info is 0.1.0+636e39b (mtools 636e39b9, 2026-11-05), an ancestor of the W2346 landing, so the pinned commit path lacks stackempty and clause R's rework. | 2026-11-08T00:26:24Z: 2026-11-07 THE RACE, NAMED FROM THE CODE (nothing changed yet). WHERE THE REQUEST IS READ: the withdraw marker (commit_withdraw.marker_path, withdraw-<key> beside commit.counts) is read in exactly ONE place, phase() in .githooks/pre-commit (line 148), at the START of each gate phase; if present it removes the marker and exits 75. Nothing else reads it: commit_kata only builds its path (line 1476) and clear_marker removes it when the run ends (line 1484). WHERE IT IS WRITTEN: commit_withdraw._ask_to_stop writes the marker and SIGINTs any bazel client among the submission's descendants, then returns exit 0 'WITHDRAW REQUESTED ... stops at the next phase boundary' for EVERY in-flight row (state == INFLIGHT), without asking whether another phase() call remains. THE RACE: a request that arrives after the gate's last phase() call has no reader. The gate runs to its end, the stack lands from the files FROZEN AT SUBMIT (stacksnap), and clear_marker then deletes the unread marker, so the request is accepted with exit 0 and silently discarded. That is the shape of 0ed0fe0b (requested ~23:45Z, landed, carrying a file the session had since deleted) and 561bb7e4. A second, smaller window: the request lands between the last phase() and the landing step even when the gate has phases left to run later. THE FIX SHAPE (not built): withdraw must know whether a boundary remains. The gate already records phase marks (gatephase); read the current phase and the count of phases after it; refuse with exit 4 and 'too late: past the last boundary, will land' (W2142's wording) when none remains; and the landing step should re-check the marker once immediately before apply so that a request accepted before it holds. Witness for a build: a planted gate whose marker is written after the last phase() lands, to be refused at request time; and one written before it, to stop. | 2026-11-08T00:27:42Z: 2026-11-07 github-14 on the fix shape: reading phase marks (or a re-check) still leaves a window (withdraw reads a boundary remains, the gate passes it, the re-check runs just before the marker lands). MAKE IT ONE ATOMIC DECISION BOTH SIDES TAKE: the landing CLAIMS the stack by an atomic rename or lock on the marker path immediately before apply, and withdraw tries the same claim; whoever wins decides, and withdraw reports which: 'withdrawn' or 'too late, will land' with exit 4. Do NOT key it on phase marks (they only estimate). Per the races ruling BRING a happens-before argument and a FORCED-INTERLEAVING WITNESS that pauses landing between its claim and apply, and between the last phase and the claim, showing each order gives one true answer. Build after b59. | 2026-11-14T12:40:38Z: 2026-11-14: RELATION TO b66 (W2378): b66's withdraw_settled makes --withdraw WAIT for the entry to leave the live map and then say LANDED <repo> <sha7> (withdraw too late) exit 5, WITHDRAWN exit 0 only when HEAD and the log were read and nothing landed, or UNKNOWN exit 7. That is an honest report AFTER the fact; it does not make the request refuse at request time or hold, so this card's atomic claim (the landing and withdraw both try one rename or lock on the marker path, whoever wins decides) is still open and builds on the same commit_withdraw.py and commit_kata.py that b66 edits whole. It follows b66, with the happens-before argument and the forced-interleaving witness the card requires.
