waypoints.title: Design to github-14: the kine-latency guard freezes and resumes a gate instead of killing it, its 4.0 s threshold learned from the series, each trip stored as a record (agree owner with luthen)
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-08T03:14:05Z: 2026-11-08: PROVENANCE. Freeze-and-resume rather than kill is github-14's design proposal on its merits (a kill at minute 3 of a latency stretch wastes the whole run; a freeze loses nothing), NOT an operator ruling: github-14 found no operator line for it in the host transcript and has asked luthen for its source. The W2036/W2028 cites were luthen's and are unrelated cards here. Treat as proposal until a source is produced. The learned-threshold and trip-record parts rest on the learned-baselines rule. | 2026-11-08T03:17:06Z: 2026-11-08 CORRECTION of my provenance note above: the freeze ruling IS the operator's, read by me in luthen's transcript (session 32b6fca1) at line 384529, uuid 6dd5f59a, 2026-11-05T14:43:43Z, origin human: 'A blend of 3 and 4 sounds right, tbh. Kinda like OOMkill, but freeze, resume when drum says it is OK.' and line 384547, uuid 214952bf, 2026-11-05T14:44:22Z: '(though resuming needs priority over spawning)'. This card EXTENDS luthen-observability:W2036 (the ask to mtools, blocked on mtools 51 ticks, unclaimed here until now), not a restart. REQUIREMENTS: (a) on a trip SIGSTOP the target bazel, SIGCONT when drum says OK; (b) a resume takes priority over admitting new spawns. ORDER: W2378 is first among the hooks-lane cards released after W2356. | 2026-11-13T19:43:05Z: 2026-11-13 READ hooks/src/mikemol/hooks/commit_withdraw.py (133 lines) and its one call site, commit_kata.py:1151. WHERE THE DEFECT IS: _ask_to_stop (94-108) for an INFLIGHT row writes the marker, interrupts the bazel client, and RETURNS at once with exit 0 and 'WITHDRAW REQUESTED <key>: its gate stops at the next phase boundary' (STOPS_AT) or '... its bazel client was interrupted'. The marker is only read at a phase boundary and the bazel interrupt only works in the bazel phase, so a gate already past its last boundary (the commit phase) ignores both and lands, while the reply said it would stop: an INTENT returned as if an outcome. A queued (not in-flight) row is different and fine: SIGTERM and 'WITHDRAWN key (waypoints)'. DESIGN: after asking, wait until the key leaves the live map (live(path, probe), an event, no wall-clock bound), then print ONE verdict line in the commit grammar: WITHDRAWN <repo> <key> when HEAD did not move or no commit names the submission's waypoints, or LANDED <repo> <sha7> (withdraw too late) when one does; exit 0 for WITHDRAWN and a distinct nonzero for LANDED. The call site has the repo root (commit_kata:1146), which commit_withdraw lacks (it gets only the commit.counts path), so root and a git runner must be injected; read HEAD before asking, git log before..HEAD after. OPEN: (1) the verdict log (verdictlog.py) is parsed from the SUBMITTER'S output and shipped to a store, not keyed by submission key and not local, so git is the local witness; (2) matching a landed commit to the submission by its waypoint symbols is a heuristic (W2219 companions recur across stacks), so prefer the first waypoint plus the HEAD-before bound; (3) release_trees runs only on exit 0, so a LANDED exit must still release the trees or it leaks them. waypoints.title: Codon does not resolve an absolute sibling import from inside a package __init__ (mikemol.rulerseq), find the idiom it accepts
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-14T20:57:30Z: 2026-11-14 no commit: a measurement, through hooks codon_probe (pinned Codon from the MODULE.bazel pin) over a scratch copy of mikemol.rulerseq beside a mikemol/__init__.py, in the session scratchpad (codon-w2431). REPRODUCED: 'import mikemol.rulerseq' fails at __init__.py:12 'no module named mikemol.rulerseq.ruler' although ruler.py is there. VARIANT 1, relative imports in __init__ ('from .ruler import (...)'): line 12 passes and the error moves to line 24, the other absolute import ('from mikemol.rulerseq.selftest import main'). VARIANT 2, that one relative too: the error moves into selftest.py:11, the same absolute import form 'from mikemol.rulerseq.ruler import (' inside a SUBMODULE: so the quirk is NOT specific to __init__, it is any absolute import of a sibling module by its full dotted name from inside its own package. VARIANT 3, selftest's import relative too: the probe prints nothing and exits 0, mikemol.rulerseq compiles. THE IDIOM CODON ACCEPTS: a single-dot relative import of a sibling ('from .ruler import X'); it resolves, the full dotted absolute form does not. House lint allows it: ruff TID252 bans only PARENT relative imports by default, and 'ruff check --config rulerseq/pyproject.toml' (select ALL) passed on the relative version. No pycodemod verb exists for it (grep of pycodemod/cli.py for relative: none). CARDED: W2507 (the verb, pilot on rulerseq), W2508 (the websubset idiom count for W1319); both enable W1319. | 2026-11-14T21:52:05Z: 2026-11-14 CORRECTION: 'mikemol.rulerseq compiles' above means codon_probe's silent pass, which is a TYPE CHECK only (found while executing W2515: probe passes code that aborts the code generator). Tools: Codon v0.20.3 (the MODULE.bazel pin, sha256 8716e5753a44...) through hooks codon_probe, 'compiles' meaning the probe printed nothing and exited 0 (compiled, NOT executed); ruff 0.16.6 with rulerseq/pyproject.toml (select ALL). Scratch files in the session scratchpad dir codon-w2512, each with the house header and docstrings so only the variant is at issue. VARIANT | CODON | RUFF: control int | None | FAIL 'unsupported operand type(s) for |' | pass. control Optional[int] | pass | FAIL non-pep604-annotation-optional. V1 two dataclasses + typing.Union | FAIL 'no module named dataclasses' | FAIL non-pep604-annotation-union. V2 two plain classes + typing.Union | pass | FAIL non-pep604-annotation-union. V3 one tagged class with a bool positional arg | pass | FAIL boolean-type-hint-positional-argument and boolean-positional-value-in-call. V3b the same with keyword-only args | FAIL 'unexpected dedent' (the bare *, wall, W1340) | pass. V4 check function plus get function, docstring documenting a Raises it does not raise | pass | FAIL docstring-extraneous-exception. V4b the same with the docstring matching the code | pass | PASS. V5 total default (an empty list from dict.get) | pass | PASS. V6 raise at the boundary (a LookupError subclass) | pass | PASS. V7 Enum tag plus a value | FAIL 'no module named enum' | pass. V8 base class plus two subclasses, concrete base | pass | FAIL no-self-use. V8b abstract base, Missing returns a constant | pass | FAIL no-self-use on Missing. V8c abstract base (raises NotImplementedError), Found holds its value, Missing holds its default | pass | PASS. RESULT: four forms pass BOTH, one per elimination option: always-present value V5, raise at the boundary V6, check/get split V4b, and the explicit two-variant result V8c (a base class and two subclasses, no Union, no dataclass, no Enum, no bool flag, no keyword-only star). Every other spelling of a two-variant result fails one side: Union fails the lint, | fails Codon, dataclass and Enum are missing stdlib modules, a bool flag fails FBT, keyword-only fails Codon. CAVEAT: compiled, not run; polymorphic dispatch under Codon's runtime is not exercised. | 2026-11-14T21:52:05Z: 2026-11-14 CORRECTION (see W2515): the 'compiles' column above is only codon_probe's TYPE CHECK, not code generation or execution. waypoints.title: Probe by execution what the pinned Codon synthesizes natively for an annotated class: init, eq, repr, ordering, hash, a frozen equivalent, and its own decorators such as tuple
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-14T22:01:51Z: 2026-11-14 no commit: a measurement, BY EXECUTION (codon run, pinned Codon v0.20.3 binary), scratch files in the session scratchpad codon-w2522. MATRIX (CPython 3.13 behaviour in brackets where it differs). PLAIN annotated class: init RUNS (positional, field order); eq FAILS ('unsupported operand type(s) for ==: P and P'); repr RUNS but is a bare object address; ordering FAILS ('unsupported operand for <'); hash FAILS ('P object has no attribute __hash__'). Codon @dataclass with NO import: the decorator is accepted, init runs, eq FAILS exactly as the plain class (it adds nothing); @dataclass(frozen=True) FAILS 'class decorator got unexpected argument' (the W1341 wall); 'from dataclasses import dataclass' FAILS 'no module named dataclasses'. Codon @tuple (a built-in, immutable): init RUNS, eq RUNS (True and False correctly), repr RUNS as '(x: 1, y: 2)' [CPython dataclass prints P(x=1, y=2)], ordering RUNS ('<' True), hash RUNS (and returns a value for an instance with a LIST field, where CPython raises TypeError: unhashable type list); IMMUTABLE: assigning a field is a COMPILE error 'cannot modify tuple attributes' (the frozen equivalent); defaults WORK (y: int = 7, P(1).y is 7); a List[int] field works and eq compares it elementwise; a MUTABLE default (items: List[int] = []) is SHARED across instances (appending to a.items changes b.items), so there is NO native default_factory. USER CLASS DECORATORS: 'def deco(cls): return cls' then '@deco' FAILS 'unsupported class decorator', so a single-source decorator FUNCTION cannot work under Codon. CONSEQUENCES for the design (W2523): the Codon target for frozen+eq+order+hash is its built-in @tuple, NOT a decorator function; a spelling valid in CPython (a marker the module defines) must be rewritten to @tuple in a STAGED COPY (the part Codon cannot express, which github-cb allowed), or the single-source module is CPython-only plus a codegen step; default_factory needs a constructor wrapper because @tuple shares mutable defaults; repr format and list-field hashing differ from CPython and the shared test suite (W2524) must pin which behaviour is the contract.

waypoints.title: Design a single-source mikemol dist whose dataclass decorator works under CPython, mypy strict, ruff select-ALL and codon run, scoped to frozen, eq, order, default, default_factory and field order
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Write the design note (the lowering table: source dataclass argument and field forms to @tuple output or a named refusal), then the pycodemod verb with a dry run and the suite (W2524).
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-14T22:04:12Z: 2026-11-14 DESIGN POINTS from github-cb (direction: the SOURCE keeps stdlib @dataclass(frozen=True) for CPython, mypy and ruff, and the STAGED COPY lowers it to @tuple; that may mean NO new runtime module at all), with the probes they asked for, BY EXECUTION on the pinned Codon 0.20.3 (scratchpad codon-w2522). (1) HASH DIVERGENCE: a frozen class with an unhashable field (list, dict, set) hashes under Codon (measured: returns a value) and raises TypeError under CPython, so the rewrite REFUSES it with a named error; the source fix is a tuple or frozenset field; suite mutant: a list field must be refused. (2) REPR: @tuple ACCEPTS a __repr__ override (measured: prints P(x=1, y=2), repr() the same), so the rewrite emits the CPython form; no 'repr non-contractual' needed. (3) MUTABLE DEFAULTS: CPython already refuses list defaults, so only default_factory reaches the rewrite. waypoints.title: Design: the bazel-admit nominal 4096 MB hold throttles the fleet at a fake resource edge; zram is the real gate

Evidence: bazel test holds 4096 (bazel_admit.py:127, docstring calls it a nominal weight) against TOTAL_MB min(70% MemTotal, 8192) set once at ledger creation (admit.py:972-973), never re-derived; host 126 GiB, ~40 GiB available, zram 11%; el-openglo waits on 'need 4096 free 1784'; ~23 substrate 64 MB selftests sit behind the head-of-line 4096 bazel WAIT. Rulings: operator line 17090 uuid 27826e27 (membudget waits for zram within a safe range, not for a lease), line 17912 (admission check before the executor copies into zram); memory project-guardrails-within-which-novelty-pumps l.17 (budget sized from current available memory and its trend; fix the control law, not the number). Shape: (1) bazel hold 0 MB so zram is its only gate (W837); any byte budget comes from a published series with its trend, never one MemAvailable read; (2) engagement metric (holds per reason, duration) with an autocalibrated alert; (3) head-of-line only for real capacity waits; (4) audit fleet callers setting BAZEL_ADMIT_MAX_WAIT_S (becomes a wall-clock MEMBUDGET_TIMEOUT, bazel_admit.py:236-237, against the no-wall-clock rule). waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-16T22:17:15Z: 2026-11-16 github-cb on the design (answer with a WITNESS, not an argument): (a) name the original flood, the 2026-10-05 zram-full outage, and the card or row that added the nominal hold; (b) show whether the zram gate alone would have held those starts, noting it samples zram BEFORE a start, not during a run (operator line 17912: 'catch actions as they're about to begin'); (c) if it would not have, the fix is a gate keyed to zram's TREND or to bytes about to enter zram, not a return to a typed constant. | 2026-11-17T20:24:00Z: 2026-11-17 ANSWER TO github-cb's (a), READ FROM GIT AND CODE: THE FLOOD was the 2026-10-05 outage: a session that skipped the manual 'read the zram fact before heavy bazel work' pointer filled zram1, which remounted /var/tmp read-only and killed every shell command. THE CARD AND COMMIT that added the hold: W836, commit 3e875dc1 (2026-10-06), 'hooks: bazel admits or waits on the host's resources itself, through its own tools/bazel wrapper' (operator 2026-10-06: integrate the zram pointer into bazel itself as an admit-or-wait gate). WHAT IT ADDED: mikemol-bazel-admit waits while zram is at or above host_facts.REFUSE_FRACTION (bounded, exit 3 after the wait), then runs under a membudget HOLD (not run: run would cap the bazel server daemon's cgroup, measured MemoryMax=4096M); the commit message calls the lease's MB incidental, and bazel_admit.py:20 and :127 (HEAVY_MB = build/test/coverage 4096, run 2048, fetch 1024) call it a nominal weight, not a claim about what bazel will use. (b) MY READING, NOT A MEASUREMENT: the gate checks zram BEFORE a start, so N starts admitted while zram reads low all begin together and fill it (the 2026-10-05 shape); the 4096 hold against TOTAL_MB = min(70 percent of MemTotal, 8192) (admit.py:972-973) is what limits heavy bazel to TWO at a time on this 126 GiB host. So the nominal hold is acting as a CONCURRENCY CAP standing in for a missing trend gate, which is why removing it (this card's shape 1) would reopen the original race unless a gate keyed to zram's TREND or to the bytes about to enter zram replaces it first (github-cb's (c)). WITNESS STILL OWED for (b): a rehearsal that starts K heavy bazel clients against a zram gate with no hold, on a measured-low zram, and reads the peak zram; not run (it risks the outage it models, so it needs a small zram or a stand-in). ORDER IMPLIED FOR THE DESIGN: first the trend or bytes-about-to-enter gate and its engagement metric, then the hold to 0, never the reverse.

waypoints.title: Watchdog: a --status read mode showing liveness over a window, 'not confirmed live' rather than 'dead'
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Send github-cb the blobs (watchdog.py 825b0608, test_watchdog.py 42e26771, warrants.bib 66360525, sites BUILD 6dee5836) and invocation f68b60da; github-cb is the reviewer who asked for this for the unfreeze review. waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-17T21:29:53Z: 2026-11-17 BUILT AND WITNESSED IN SCRATCH (mtools-W2618, not landed). FINDING FIRST: nothing a running watchdog left could show it was POLLING. watchdog.pid names a process (a signal-0 probe says it exists) and watchdog.last is the explanation of its last EXIT; the armed gauge goes to the store, not to a file a reader compares. A live pid is not a polling loop, so the 'advanced across a window' read the card asks for needed a monotone mark the watch loop writes. BUILD (hooks/src/mikemol/hooks/watchdog.py): holder(git_dir) reads the pid file (0 when absent, unreadable or not a number; running() now tests pid != 0 first, since a signal-0 probe of pid 0 reaches this process's whole group); a pulse file .git/mtools/watchdog.pulse {pid, poll, poll_s} replaced whole (written beside itself, renamed over) by beat_pulse, read by read_pulse (NO_PULSE = (0, -1, 0.0) for absent, garbage, non-object, missing field, wrong type or a bool); pulsing_sleep(git_dir, pid, poll_s, sleep) writes pulse 0 at start and the next count before each poll's own sleep, so watch() IS UNCHANGED and a watchdog stuck inside a read or a ready-count never reaches it; status(git_dir, window_s, sleep, alive) reads the pid file, then the pulse, sleeps the window, reads again, and returns (True, 'live (advanced): pid N polled K time(s) in Ws, now at poll P') only when the count rose from the pid that holds the file; every other case is 'not confirmed live: <reason>' (no pid file, a dead pid, a live pid with no pulse, another pid's pulse, a pulse that did not move, and when the window is not longer than the watchdog's own poll the line says a still pulse proves nothing and names a longer window); never 'dead'. CLI: mikemol-watchdog --state Q --status [--window S] (default 40 s = two polls at the default poll) starts nothing, needs no writer, exits 0 confirmed, 1 not confirmed, 7 for a window that is not positive. The pulse is the watchdog's OWN file: the session heartbeat is untouched, so asking resets nothing (the watchdog module's own rule). REAL WITNESS, the card's: a real watchdog (python -m mikemol.hooks.watchdog --poll-s 1) on a scratch repo, then --status --window 3 printed 'live (advanced): pid 4166441 polled 3 time(s) in 3s, now at poll 7' (exit 0); I stopped it and the same command printed 'not confirmed live: no running watchdog holds this repo (pid 4166441 is not running)' (exit 1). TESTS: 24 new cases in tests/test_watchdog.py (round trip with no staging debris, 7 malformed pulses, an unwritable directory never raises, pulse 0 at start and one per sleep, one pulse per watch poll, advanced, first pulse during the window, still pulse, short window, no pid file / pid 0 / dead pid (alive never called for 0), no pulse / another pid's pulse, two reads a window apart, main --status exit codes, status starts nothing and needs no writer, 3 non-positive windows, main hands the watch the pulsing sleep); existing 34 still pass, 58 in all. MUTATION: the def-sites holder, running, pulse_path, beat_pulse, _count, read_pulse, status, pulsing_sleep, _report_status, _parser and main each run alone are KILLED. 16 warrants (section heartbeat); pairing 2581 functions 0 findings; mutants_gen --write regenerated only hooks/sites/.../watchdog/BUILD.bazel. BAZEL (scratch): //hooks:test_watchdog :ruff :mypy :ratchet :graph_fresh 5 of 5 PASS, invocation f68b60da-22f3-4f2c-bf5c-21525eaadd5b. BLOBS: hooks/src/mikemol/hooks/watchdog.py 825b0608a95b1feda61f1d75709f845ca8171b1b, hooks/tests/test_watchdog.py 42e2677149ef75e0381487bdeb459a78d3839e50, hooks/warrants.bib 663605257cb0571c0536bfe510a8713369fd381c, hooks/sites/src/mikemol/hooks/watchdog/BUILD.bazel 6dee58366d2fa860c4dda49cfa2412f370b608ba. KNOWN LIMITS: a watchdog started BEFORE this change leaves no pulse, so its status reads 'not confirmed live ... no pulse of its own' until it is restarted (the wording says so); the pulse advances once per poll, so a window under the poll can read a live watchdog as still, which the line states. The count is NOT derived from load1: since W1776 (github-8f, 2026-10-20) jobs = max(MIN_JOBS=2, min(cores, round(cores - busy))) where busy is the fraction of /proc/stat ticks that were not idle or iowait between two reads SAMPLE_S=2 s apart, times the core count; load1 is printed for information only (the module header says why: load1 counts runnable bursts and read 47-62 on a 24-core host with 11.5 cores idle, which pinned a gate at --jobs=2 for hours). So 'jobs=2 cores=24 load1=233.74 floor=2 (held at the floor)' means about 22 or more of 24 cores were BUSY in the 2 s window (cores - busy < 2), and the floor held; load1=233.74 is a display. waypoints.title: Measure card-change events per day to derive the pack trigger
waypoints.next_bounded_step: When github-cb rules on the amortizing trigger (letter in the host inbox, 2026-11-17, item 3.2): wire the two runtime measurements (loose-fold cost per record, compaction cost) into the writer's compaction verb behind W2662's pack.problems check.
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-17T20:14:07Z: 2026-11-17 MEASURED (scratchpad scripts, read-only on the queue, throwaway repos on disk, not zram): (1) CARD-CHANGE EVENTS per day, a LOWER BOUND from consecutive committed versions of the state file since 2026-10-18 (229 commits on 19 distinct days; a field changed twice between two commits counts once, and the queue was committed on only 19 of 30 days): 7,545 field changes and 1,049 new cards; a new card is about 10 fields, so about 17,000 records over the 30 days, about 570 a day, plus the ledger (7,767 lines over 59 days, about 132 a day): about 700 loose records a day for THIS repo, about 255,000 a year. (2) READ COST of N loose files against one pack of the same records, warm page cache, same fold result: N=1,000 loose 0.066 CPU-s vs packed 0.008; N=5,000 0.219 vs 0.041; N=20,000 0.739 vs 0.171: about 37 microseconds a record loose, 8.5 packed (4 to 8 times). (3) GIT COST over N loose files: git add of N new files 0.34 s at 2,000, 1.77 s at 10,000, 4.73 s at 40,000 (about 120 microseconds a file); git status over the committed files 0.02, 0.05, 0.14 s; after compaction add of the deletions 0.06 s at 10,000 and 0.32 s at 40,000; commit of an unchanged-size tree 0.01 s. (4) INODES: /home is btrfs (df -i reports no fixed count), /var/tmp is zram1 with 16.8M inodes at 5 percent; so no inode wall is near, the cost is metadata and git's per-file work. FINDING: THERE IS NO CPU KNEE: every cost is linear and small (a year of loose records folds in about 9 s against 2 s packed), so a threshold cannot be DERIVED from a knee; a trigger needs a stated budget. PROPOSAL for the trigger, derived and not typed: compact when the extra read cost accumulated since the last compaction (loose records times the 29 microsecond difference times the number of folds since) first exceeds the measured cost of compacting, so the rule amortizes itself from two measurements the writer takes at runtime. DESIGN: pathsforward/humanhold.py (new): ASK = ^\s*operator\s*:\s*(decide|act)\s+\S, case-blind, so the verb must be followed by the question or the command (a bare 'operator: decide' is no ask, as a bare 'operator' is none in nemik); refusal(sym, blocked_on) names both forms and what was given. ops._refuse_made_hold(sym, old, new) runs after the generic 'blocked needs a party' refusal and before the card is written: a resulting human hold is judged only when it is being MADE, that is the card was not a human hold before, or it already was and the update adds an entry that is not a card reference (is_reference: W<n> or repo:W<n>). WHY 'MADE' AND NOT 'ANY UPDATE': my first cut judged every update that set the kind or the blockers, and the pathsforward suite caught three tests; reading gate.py then showed the worse one nobody tested: --gate-red appends the gate card to EVERY open waypoint with the card's own kind, so a card already on a legacy prose human hold would have refused the sweep and broken --gate-red. waypoints.title: A pinned mikemol-githook-pre-merge-commit refuses a merge into main whose resulting tree did not pass the full gate

On a ruling: build mikemol-githook-pre-merge-commit in the shape of githook_pre_push.py (a console script, the repo's .githooks/pre-merge-commit stub execs it, fails closed when the gate tool is absent), with decoy-repository tests that ARE the measured git facts below, then a githook row in W2665's census.
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-18T01:55:23Z: 2026-11-17 MEASURED on git 2.55.0 (a throwaway repo per scenario, hooks that record their own name and whether MERGE_HEAD exists, core.hooksPath pointed at them, global and system config off): A clean 'git merge --no-ff': pre-merge-commit RAN, merge commit made (2 parents), and the hook saw NO MERGE_HEAD (git has not written it yet), so the hook discriminates by the branch (git symbolic-ref HEAD), and the merged tree is the index (git write-tree). B the same with the hook exiting 1: merge REFUSED, HEAD unchanged, but MERGE_HEAD is LEFT BEHIND (the repo stays mid-merge; the refusal text must say git merge --abort). C FAST-FORWARD ('git merge feature' when main is an ancestor): NO HOOK RAN AT ALL, neither pre-merge-commit nor pre-commit, and main advanced to the feature tip: the gap the card did not name. D 'git merge --no-ff --no-commit' then 'git commit': pre-commit ran (state=merging, MERGE_HEAD present), pre-merge-commit did NOT. E CONFLICTED merge: no hook at the merge; the resolving 'git commit' ran pre-commit with MERGE_HEAD present, which ANSWERS the card's open question: a conflicted merge's commit reaches the gate through pre-commit, and pre-commit can tell it is a merge by MERGE_HEAD. F 'git merge --squash' then commit: pre-commit ran, state=none, a one-parent commit (an ordinary commit, so the branch tier applies). G --no-verify: pre-merge-commit skipped, as for pre-commit. THREE MERGE PATHS therefore, three different answers: clean non-ff merge = the NEW pre-merge-commit hook; conflicted or --no-commit merge = the EXISTING pre-commit, provided its main tier applies when MERGE_HEAD exists; fast-forward = NOTHING, and only a reference-transaction hook (every local ref update, prepared and committed phases, stdin 'old new ref') or pinning branch.main.mergeOptions=--no-ff covers it (an explicit --ff-only still bypasses the config). WIRING, read: mtools ships shared git hooks as console scripts (mikemol-githook-pre-push, -post-commit, -prepare-commit-msg in hooks/pyproject.toml) and a repo's .githooks/<name> stub execs one; pre-push is the model (fails closed, an extension point .githooks/pre-push.local). NOT READ: how a hook can know a tree already passed the full gate (the stack tree refs in stacktree.py and the commit marker are candidates), and gcalculus's own pre-commit tiering. The probe is a scratch script, untracked; its scenarios become the hook's decoy-repository tests when it is built.

waypoints.title: structural-query: decide whether git show REV:path, git cat-file -p and git blame over a claimed artifact are textual reads
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-17T23:35:26Z: DECIDED 2026-11-17: ADD NO GIT SUBCOMMAND BEYOND grep. no commit: a decision record, the measurement below is the evidence (scratchpad git_readers.py, run in scratch mtools-W2616, which carries W2616's git grep reader, against the project's real claim table). MEASURED: the claim table has 5 claims (.htm .html .md .mht .mhtml; .py is NOT claimed here). Twenty git command shapes run over a CLAIMED path (INSTALL.md) and an UNCLAIMED one (a .py file, the control): ONLY git grep over the claimed path is refused today; show REV:path, show REV~N:path, cat-file -p, cat-file blob, blame, annotate, log -p, log -S, diff REV -- path are all admitted, and so are the ones that must stay admitted (add, status, diff --stat, ls-files, rev-parse REV:path, ls-tree, log --oneline, show -s, cat-file -s, cat-file -t); no shape is refused over the unclaimed path, so there is no false positive to explain. ROUTES: the refusal must name a tool that answers the same question. mdstruct's read modes (spans, budget, items, grep, tables, rows, classify, labels, roundtrip, fixpoint, lint, verify, narrowest) take a FILE or a directory in the WORKING TREE, and its stdin form (--body-file -) exists only for the write modes; mikemol-htmlstruct (outline, links, tables, meta, text, parts, part) takes a FILE. Neither reads a revision. So show REV:path, cat-file -p/blob, blame, annotate and log -p over a claimed file have NO structural twin: a refusal would route to a tool that reads the CURRENT file, which answers a different question (what the file is now, not what it was at REV, who wrote a line, or what a commit changed). The card's own rule, 'add only the subcommands that have a route', therefore adds none. REJECTED, kept so it is not re-proposed: widening _GIT_TEXTUAL to show, cat-file, blame, annotate, log; reason: no route, and the roster's own notes call an over-inclusion a refusal of work that was never the problem. KNOWN LIMIT OF W2616, found here: git grep PATTERN REV -- FILE.md reads a revision and its refusal routes to mdstruct grep over the working-tree file, a different question; not changed, since the pattern-search shape is the one the refusal was built for. REVISIT ONLY IF mdstruct or htmlstruct gains a mode that reads a revision's bytes: then the three shapes have a route and the measurement is a one-line rerun.

waypoints.title: Prove early cutoff in isolation: an AST-normalized copy of procrun's sources is byte-identical across a comment-only edit, so an action downstream of it does not re-run
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-18T01:45:30Z: 2026-11-17: MINTED by atomizing W2262: its design note (.claude/design/W2262-diamond-targets.md, preserved at 219b33a8 and c45228f8 after the clean-up, no longer in the working tree) names the one mechanism to prove first, and W2261's measurement (a comment in a leaf re-runs the whole dist's tests) gives its success test. The key insight behind the spike: the design wants X_c content-stable under a comment-only change, and an AST-normalized copy of X's sources is exactly that, deterministic and comment-insensitive; whether bazel's action cache cuts off downstream on an identical output is the thing to MEASURE, not assume. | 2026-11-18T01:47:36Z: 2026-11-17 SPIKE RESULT 1 (scratch mtools-W2718, procrun only, base a365e9a7, NOT for landing): the mechanism holds in isolation. Files: procrun/normalize_tool.py (ast.parse then ast.unparse, docstrings kept, comments and formatting dropped), procrun/normalize.bzl (rule normalized_py: one NormalizePy action per source with the copies as declared outputs; rule normalized_digest: one action that sha256sums the copies, the stand-in for a dependent), procrun/BUILD.bazel (py_binary normalize_tool, normalized_py norm over the dist's sources, normalized_digest norm_digest). MEASURED with bazel build //procrun:norm_digest (the 'N processes' line; linux-sandbox count = actions that RAN): A cold: 4 sandboxed, 21eab905-87b9-4006-887d-1d8e64e01f8c; B unchanged: 0 sandboxed, 11 action cache hits, b88685f6-e0ac-4874-9e23-96e6c84b4459; C a comment line plus the blank lines ruff-format requires appended to proc.py: 1 sandboxed (the NormalizePy of proc.py) and the digest consumer an action cache hit, so EARLY CUTOFF HELD, 08214841-6092-452b-8486-5630e4e10ed2; D CONTROL, a new function in proc.py: 2 sandboxed (the normalizer and the consumer), 7e8c9138-5edc-4cf7-b1b6-b56ff76b6d0b; E source restored: 0 sandboxed, 2 disk cache hits, 8fa6d8a3-5701-418f-a8ad-5a27a7ff04f5; git status shows proc.py clean. So the discriminator holds: a real change re-runs the consumer, a comment-or-whitespace change does not. WHAT IS CUT OFF: any edit whose parse tree is unchanged (comments, blank lines, layout, quote style, redundant parentheses); NOT cut off: a docstring edit (kept), a rename, a new definition. COSTS AND LIMITS, stated now so they are not discovered later: (1) ast.unparse drops comments, so a '# type: ignore' or '# noqa' that mypy or ruff reads is lost: the normalized copy is for RUNNING a dependent's tests, never for type-checking or linting; (2) tracebacks and __file__ in a dependent's test point into normalized text, so line numbers differ from the real source; (3) the output is stable only within one interpreter version (the hermetic bazel toolchain pins it); (4) ruff-format's own rule forced two blank lines before my probe comment, so the probe is a comment-plus-whitespace edit, which is the realistic case. NOT YET SHOWN: a dependent's TEST action running against the normalized copies and not re-running (the second step, measuring memres against normalized procrun, is running now). | 2026-11-18T01:53:46Z: 2026-11-17 SPIKE RESULT 2 (the decisive one), same scratch tree mtools-W2718, memres as the dependent, same probe (a comment line plus the blank lines ruff-format requires, appended to procrun/src/mikemol/procrun/proc.py), bazel test //memres:all, 34 targets. CONTROL, memres on the real //procrun:procrun: 29 of 34 re-ran, f9dafff3-d164-4559-b1ad-63cbf5eae62c (baseline before it 34 of 34, 4bfac3eb-b577-4777-97bd-738562908f18). WITH memres's library and its 13 tests depending on //procrun:procrun_norm (a py_library over the normalized copies, imports normalized/procrun/src): baseline 34 of 34 PASS (14 executed, the rest cached), f7ebd3d8-7786-49bf-94d6-6dd57759150a, so the tests run correctly against normalized procrun; then the probe with a FRESH comment text: 16 of 34 re-ran, 148ec565-6671-48d8-a49f-d5f575cffc1e. DISCLOSED: my first probe repeated the control's exact edit and read 0 of 34 (6ca5af39-d8fd-41b6-a87c-b2a4537a727f); that is NOT evidence, because the targets still on real procrun were answered from the disk cache by the control's identical keys, so I redid it with new text. WHAT THE 16 ARE, by bazel query (a label query says all 29 still reach proc.py, through the normalizer rule; the action graph is what cuts off): all 13 unit tests were CUT OFF, and the 16 that re-ran are the 12 mutation shards, mypy, ratchet, ratchet_refusal and venv, the targets that consume real procrun (mypy_runner deps and the .venv srcs name //procrun:procrun; the grid runs under :.venv). 29 minus 13 equals 16, so the account closes. RESULT: pointing a dependent's tests at an AST-normalized copy of a dependency removes every unit-test re-run for a comment-or-whitespace edit in the dependency (13 of 13 here), at the cost of nothing the tests can see. FILES (blobs; a SPIKE, not for landing as it stands): procrun/BUILD.bazel ec55bf908c784855e7fcfbe690cd3bf631dab829, procrun/normalize.bzl 2d65a1258e0d68462f788c6b1e07deae286e9887, procrun/normalize_tool.py ba6e03b4485f8bef6f6ebac51dcfd8d5ad2c56ed, memres/BUILD.bazel 8c50739c074e0bd4f720c9db42cad1993bc5390c (memres deps re-pointed in two places: the library and the test loop); proc.py restored, git status shows only these four. NEXT STEPS, each a design question for W2262, not built: (a) the 12 mutation shards and venv could take the normalized copy too (the grid mutates memres, not procrun), which would cut 13 more; (b) mypy needs the real source or a stub: a SIGNATURES-ONLY artifact (an .pyi derived from the parse tree, bodies and docstrings dropped) is the interface digest proper, and would also cut a body-only change from a dependent's mypy; (c) the rule as a macro for every dist, with a switch per dependent edge (design constraint 3, declared per object); (d) combine with W2717's per-module libraries so a change in one of a dependency's modules cuts off at module granularity. LIMITS stand from result 1: a normalized copy loses comments mypy and ruff read, tracebacks cite normalized line numbers, and the output is stable within one interpreter version.

waypoints.title: mikemol-watchdog takes attachable event sources and wakes the session with the event named, instead of waiting out its window
waypoints.next_bounded_step: DESIGN TO github-b0 FIRST, ranked behind the W2665 chain (W2573 first). Operator 2026-11-18 via github-b0: 'ask for the watchdog to accept event attachments from the nemik/pathsforward infrastructure; anything anyone checks on after waking is something the watchdog should be more proactive about.' Event sources named: a peer's review ref appearing, an inbound row naming this session, a witness turning true, a gate verdict landing, a card this session is blocked on going done. Design points to settle: (1) the source interface (a named observer returning a stable event key and a one-line text; fixed and declared, not a shell command, as nemik's witnesses are); (2) which sources reuse nemik's observers (nemik-inbound, nemik-witnesses facts) and which are mtools' own (the writer's blocked_on going done); (3) fire-once semantics, so an event wakes the session once and a restart does not replay it; (4) the exit code and line: exit 8 names the event so the session reads what to do; (5) cost: sources polled on the watchdog's own poll, never a wall timer. DEPENDS on the event list from the transcript-review card, which says what sessions actually check on after waking. W1472 is the idle-watchdog design card this extends.
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-18T17:20:14Z: 2026-11-18 DESIGN POINT from github-b0 (host): the heartbeat moves only on WRITER use, so a session busy messaging peers and reading reviews reads as idle and is woken for nothing. Message sends (SendMessage) and review reads are activity too, so they must count as beats. Mechanism to design with the event sources: a beat from the PostToolUse hook for those tools (the beat hook exists, mikemol-hook-beat, and writes the heartbeat on every tool call where wired), not a poll; note the wake lines on this host today read 'last heartbeat 903s ago (mikemol-paths-forward)' and 'hook:Bash', i.e. the hook beat is already read where it is wired, so check which tools the host's settings wire it on before adding anything. Related defect carded on W2690 (the restart text prints the wrong program and drops the window flags).

waypoints.title: The round check at submit does not count transitive demand and reads a ready state the queue does not hold, so a wired gate-repair chain is refused
waypoints.next_bounded_step: VELOCITY DEFECT, found by b90 (2026-11-18), four refusals with identical text on rounds written after the chain was wired. EXACT TEXT of the last: 'NOT COMMITTED mtools: this stack is refused at submit, before it waits: W2696, W2421 are in this repository's round and ready, but the working set includes W2632, W2636, W2640, which is not: take W2696 first with mikemol-paths-forward --state .claude/paths-forward.json --update W2696 --status working; then W2421, each the same way'. FACTS: (1) the queue holds W2632, W2636, W2640, W2694, W2696 and W2421 all as status working, yet the check calls W2696 and W2421 ready, and earlier called W2694 ready: it reads a state other than the queue's status field (read hooks/src/mikemol/hooks/round_wire.py refusals() and the round file's row fields to name which). (2) after W2694 became entry 4's waypoint, it stopped being named, so the refusal is about the stack's waypoint list. (3) W2632, W2636, W2640 each enable W2680, W2680 enables W2681 to W2682 to W2683 to W2573 to W2665 (R:C, W:Y, weights synced twice), and the check still says they are not in the round: it does not count demand that flows through edges. FIX TO DESIGN (to github-b0 first): the round membership the check consults must include cards that enable a round card transitively, or the check must say which field it reads; and a card marked working must not read ready. Failing test first on round_wire with a fixture round whose ready set is two cards and a stack whose cards reach one of them by edges.
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-18T13:48:30Z: 2026-11-18 SOURCE READ (hooks/src/mikemol/hooks): (1) NO gate-repair exemption exists: commit_kata.py line 1233 calls _round_refusal(root, stack_cards(stack_file)) unconditionally in the submit refusal chain, and round_wire.py's only exemption is the W2219 co-lander (CO_LANDER at line 221, as_submitted line 261 to 262); the word gate-repair appears nowhere on the submit path. (2) 'READY' IS BY DESIGN, not a state mismatch: round_wire._submitted_status (lines 224 to 240) returns working for cards of the stack and ready for ANY OTHER working card ('a mark says nothing at submit', as_submitted docstring lines 246 to 250), so W2696 and W2421 read ready because they are working cards outside the stack. (3) THE ROUND for mtools (round.json 13:47:47Z, nemik's top three ready cards per repo): W2694 rank 1 salience 3413, W2696 rank 2 salience 9, W2421 rank 3 salience 5.693. The wiring WORKED: W2694 is now the round's top card by a wide margin; W2632, W2636 and W2640 are not in the top three because the round is a fixed three per repo, and the check refuses a stack that names cards outside the round while round cards are ready and skipped. waypoints.title: State what the gate's run, admission and failed telemetry series measure, and which run-seconds family is canonical
waypoints.next_bounded_step: ANSWERED FROM THE CODE 2026-11-19 (store read-back NOT done): (1) target.cpu.seconds is user+sys. It comes from the 'shard cpu=S children=K idle_wall=W' line the mutation runner prints (check_mutants/mutate_runner.py cpu_line, line 1658, called at 1801 with resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_utime + ru_stime): CPU seconds of the runner's reaped child processes, summed, never wall; children = workers; idle_wall = cpu / children. hooks gatetargets.py reads that line from each :mutants or :test_* target's local test.log (kind_of: mutants, pytest, other); a target whose log has no shard line gets NO cpu or children row, only wall (so cpu is absent for plain pytest targets that do not print it, and 'other' kinds are never read). (2) run.emitted{repo} = the count of targets whose result RAN in this bazel invocation (cached results excluded), 0 for a fully cached gate; target.failed{target,kind,repo} = 1 when that target's final attempt did not PASS else 0, one per fresh result that carries a status; target.wall.seconds = the target's own wall seconds from the build event; admission_wait_seconds = the commit's submit to its lease (gate queue wait); (3) run.seconds and run_seconds are TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES from two emitters, not one family: mikemol.gate.run.seconds (gatetargets.py RUN_SECONDS) = the bazel invocation's wall, finished minus started event; mikemol.gate.run_seconds (commit_span.py RUN_NAME) = lease to verdict of the whole gate (pre-bazel steps included). The literal repo='repo': mikemol-gate-targets takes REPO from .githooks/pre-commit line 942, basename of MIKEMOL_REAL_ROOT or the root; a repository directory literally named 'repo' (the hook's own test fixtures, stackrun tests, create one) labels itself repo. waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-19T21:54:47Z: OPERATOR RULING 2026-11-19 via github-00: a parked preventive measure counts as velocity once something is hit that a backburnered thing would have caught. THE HIT: luthen:W2790, luthen's checks/hoststate_fence_test.py patched planflow.changes_match, which waldo 9ea5914 (this repo's W2765) removed; the test went AttributeError only under the sha's own venv, so luthen's main has been red since 5fe43617 unseen, and would have turned every luthen landing red the moment W2777 synced the venv. DESIGN SKETCH (send first): an ast pass over test files resolves every patch target (mock.patch('pkg.mod.name'), patch.object(module, 'name'), monkeypatch.setattr(module, 'name', ...)) against the module as the DECLARED packages define it and refuses one that does not exist; create=True refused unless a stated reason sits beside it (create=True is how a dead target hides). Second rung, designed even if it lands later: refuse a patch whose target exists but which the code under test never references. PLANTS: a removed name refused, a renamed name refused, create=True with no reason refused, a valid target admitted. ESTIMATE as_of 2026-11-19, basis analogue (the W2790 hit, one red main for an unmeasured number of landings), low confidence: cost ~2 attempts and ~2500 CPU-s (a pycheck-family change in a pinned dist, vendored by every repo); EFFECT on attempts per landing: prevents the red-main class, which for luthen would have refused every landing until fixed; I do not have the count of refused attempts, so the interval is a guess, 1 to 10 refused attempts per occurrence; CPU effect per occurrence 15,000 to 30,000 CPU-s per refused full gate (the interval on W2776, unmeasured here). Scope: every repo's tests. | 2026-11-19T21:56:04Z: github-00 2026-11-19: weigh an IMPORT PROBE over the AST: a bazel test whose packages are exactly the declared ones, importing the target module and asking hasattr, is sound for setattr and star-imports, and in a hermetic sandbox 'no code runs' buys little; the AST pass could stay as a fast pre-commit lint with the probe as the gate's authority. Pick by which gives a sound refusal with fewer declared exceptions. MY CHOICE for the design: the IMPORT PROBE is the authority (zero declared exceptions for import-time names, since the module is asked what it has), run in the dist's own test sandbox; the AST pass is the fast lint and, where it cannot resolve a name, it stays silent rather than refusing (it never refuses what the probe would admit). Residue the probe does not cover: a module whose import needs a resource the sandbox lacks (it refuses with the import error named, never a pass), and a name bound lazily on first use (module __getattr__), which hasattr does answer by calling it.

waypoints.title: transcriptstruct --extract replaces an attached image with a placeholder or takes --no-images (skills:W83 observation)

waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-21T23:06:07Z: 2026-11-21 BUILT on top of W2853 (300b89f8): review/W2854-extract-no-images 04da9266f8a95c67070d8666c2f2ee0bbd83ddef, parent W2853 so the diff is the delta; transcriptstruct only (cli.py, tests/test_cli.py, warrants.bib), a non-hooks stack. CHOICE: a --no-images flag on --extract, NOT a default placeholder. The decoder principle (blocks.py, test_an_unknown_block_is_kept_whole_and_marked_undecoded) is that an undecoded block is kept whole and never truncated, so a default elision would drop bytes unasked; the flag leaves every default read unchanged and lets --extract be used on a record carrying a screenshot. WHAT: --no-images replaces every base64 data string in an UNDECODED block with <N chars of base64 omitted>, keeping the other keys (the media type stays). Only an undecoded block is parsed and re-written (its text is the record own JSON); a decoded block text is prose and is never parsed, so a message that looks like JSON is left exactly as it is. Helpers _without_image_data, _elided; _extract takes a keyword elide. TEST (1, in the EXISTING test_cli.py): a record with a text block and a 5000 character image prints the base64 whole by default, and with --no-images prints <5000 chars of base64 omitted>, the text block and the media type intact. 224 transcriptstruct tests pass, pycheck admits both py files, warrants +1. NOT DONE: the bazel run at the sha (the W2853 run is still using the box), github-00 review. | 2026-11-22T00:24:22Z: 2026-11-21 PARKED. github-00 PASS-SUBMIT of W2854 r2 review/W2854-extract-no-images-r2 d69be5f9feed3505bd95c9eb0796fd5a9b9e4107 (parent r1 04da9266, W2853 300b89f8). waypoints.title: mutation runner: a suite ended as hung records its tree states and wait channels, and a control on an oversubscribed box must not time out
waypoints.next_bounded_step: On the bazel run at be64d44a send github-00 the sha and verdict; submit after b112
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-21T22:08:05Z: 2026-11-21 CAUSE READ FROM THE RUNNER SOURCE (check_mutants/mutate_runner.py), github-00 question answered. WHERE: the control prints "timed out on the UNMUTATED module" when _launch_suite raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired (lines 1386 to 1393), and launch() raises it for exactly two things: (1) _hung, a stillness witness: MUTATE_PATIENCE polls (24) of MUTATE_POLL_S (5.0 s) in a row with neither the output bytes nor the tree CPU changed, AND no process of the tree or its group in state R or D (waiting_on_host, W2642, which excuses a starved runnable process and a disk wait), and (2) SIGXCPU at MUTATE_CPU_S (120 s of CPU, an RLIMIT_CPU, a pure CPU bound). WHAT IT MEASURES: (2) is CPU and load-agnostic. (1) is a COUNT OF POLLS, but a poll is a wall interval, so it is 24 x 5 s = 120 s of wall time of genuine sleep (state S) with no output: not contention by construction, because R and D are excused. idle_wall=232.9s in the shard line is NOT a clock: it is a computed figure, shard cpu divided by children (line 1886), the wall the shard would take on an idle host. SO github-00 SUSPICION THAT THE CLOCK COUNTED WALL TIME WHILE THE CHILD SAT IDLE IS HALF RIGHT: the stillness window is wall time, but it only counts polls in which the child was in S, so an oversubscribed box does not trip it unless the child sleeps. WHAT IS STRANGE: the control test is test_judge_reviewing.py::test_a_reviewer_that_is_not_running_is_no_block, a pure in-memory call of judge_reviewing, 3 tests in 0.06 s alone (measured locally in this tree). A 0.06 s test cannot burn 120 CPU s, so (2) did not fire, and it cannot sit asleep for 120 s by itself, so (1) fired on a process that was ASLEEP in S, with no output, for 120 s, at STARTUP (import of 91 modules, pytest plugin load, the node-report plugin, or a lock). The cause is therefore NOT named: it is a start-up stall of unknown wait channel. THE FIX IS AN INSTRUMENT FIRST, as W2818 did for the killer: when _hung fires, write to the log the process states and the wait channel (/proc/<pid>/wchan and stat state) of every process of the tree, so the next stall names what it was waiting on; THEN decide the bound. A CPU-only bound is already the other half (RLIMIT_CPU) and the stillness witness is the absence detector the operator ruled for (no wall clock), so the arm to plant is the one github-00 asked: a control run beside a forced sleep or a CPU hog on an oversubscribed box must not be ended as hung while its process is R or D, and a suite that is genuinely asleep with no output for the patience still is. NOT DONE: the instrument, the arm, and whether main reproduces it (the control run on pristine main 6b54fed2 is still running). This card blocks W2833 and every pathsforward mutation verdict until it names its cause. | 2026-11-21T22:09:33Z: 2026-11-21 INSTRUMENT SPEC WIDENED (github-00): at the kill, besides each tree process state and wchan, log (1) the full /proc/<pid>/syscall line, (2) the open fds with their link targets (ls -l /proc/<pid>/fd, so a lock file or a pipe shows up), and (3) for a pipe, which process holds the other end and THAT process state. THE HYPOTHESIS TO TEST AND NOT TO BANK: a startup sleep in S under load is a wait on another process that is itself starved (an flock on a shared cache such as uv, pytest or bazel output base, or a pipe read from a producer OUTSIDE the tree). waiting_on_host looks only inside the tree and its group, so it would miss it. If the instrument shows that, the fix is to widen the witness to blocked on a runnable process ANYWHERE, not to lengthen the window (120 s of wall). The plant for the arm: a child blocked on a pipe whose writer is a CPU hog outside its tree must not be ended as hung while the writer is R, and the same child with an idle writer in S still is. | 2026-11-21T22:11:57Z: 2026-11-21 CONTROL ON PRISTINE MAIN 6b54fed2 PASSES: //pathsforward:mutants_11 passed in 440 s elapsed, BES 083ec38c-05a3-4619-b0cd-270d6c289837 (copied from the log). The same shard FAILED inside the W2833 whole-pathsforward run at 216d6639 (BES 5b78d99c-81da-4268-81ee-cabe459fa674, 742 s, control timed out on test_a_reviewer_that_is_not_running_is_no_block). W2833 changes only render.py, a test and warrants, and the failing cells are closegate, cli and reconcile cells, so main is NOT red and the failure is a FLAKE with the first cause named only as a startup stall of a 0.06 s test, wait channel unknown. The two runs differ in load: the failing run was a 195-test invocation of 6,447 s elapsed sharing the box with the b112 gate, the passing control was one shard alone. That is consistent with the oversubscription hypothesis and does not prove it. A flake is a blocker: W2833 and every pathsforward mutation verdict wait on this card. | 2026-11-21T22:21:37Z: 2026-11-21 INSTRUMENT BUILT on main 6b54fed2: review/W2863-hang-record be64d44a98a928f4a73210db9edf5ecb5c1a13c4 (check_mutants only: mutate_runner.py, test_mutate_runner.py, warrants.bib; a non-hooks stack, no shard guard). WHAT: hang_record(root, proc) returns one line, "hang record: " then per process of the tree (first 6): pid, comm, state, wchan, the /proc syscall line, and each PIPE it holds as fd=pipe:[inode]->peers pid(comm,state) of the OTHER holders anywhere on the host (up to 4); _hung takes it BEFORE the kill and attaches it with note() to the cell that was running, so cell_lines prints it after the id; waiting_on_host now shares _table and _members with it. Each fd is read on its own because the listing own directory descriptor closes mid-read (the first version lost the pipe list to that, caught by the first planted test). TESTS (3, in the EXISTING runner module, no new file), the planted pipe and hog arm github-00 asked for, by construction: (1) a child asleep on a pipe held from outside its tree reads state S, wchan anon_pipe_read, its pipe, and THIS process as the other holder; (2) the same with a CPU hog as the only other holder shows the hog as R; (3) launch with MUTATE_PATIENCE 3 ends a sleeping suite as hung and the cell note starts with hang record pid= and state=S. 145 runner tests pass, pycheck admits both py files, warrants +3. NOT A CAUSE: this names nothing about the 5b78d99c stall; it makes the NEXT stall name its wait channel, so the flake stays open and a blocker until a record shows the cause. The fix after that (widen waiting_on_host to blocked on a runnable process anywhere, or not) is decided from a record, never from load. RUN AT THE SHA: //:test_mutate_runner //:ruff //:mypy_check_mutants //procrun:mutants running. CONTROL: with the succeeding stub signer (it must emit [GNUPG:] SIG_CREATED, review finding F3) and push.gpgSign=true, git push to the bare remote succeeds and the remote records a certificate (a push-cert in its refs or a receive hook seeing GIT_PUSH_CERT); ARM: under isolated_repo the failing gpg.program makes the same push FAIL, and push.gpgSign=if-asked with no --signed does not sign. If this git or the bare remote cannot carry a push certificate the control does not show a cert and the arm REFUSES by pytest.fail naming the host fact, never passing vacuously, as arm 2 does. waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-21T23:45:58Z: 2026-11-21 FROM github-00 (review of W2865 c069cfb7, accepted as an INTERIM fix): the time comparison is a proxy and misses more than a same-second write. A committer date is whatever the committer set: a commit fetched from a peer, or one made with GIT_COMMITTER_DATE, can carry a date OLDER than the log mtime while being a different head, so the row reads fresh and is wrong. THE FIX: the waiter writes head=<sha> at LAUNCH, before the commit runs (the sha HEAD had when the verdict was started), and _verdict compares that sha with the current HEAD. Once it exists the time comparison is only the FALLBACK for old logs that have no head line, and the row says which rule judged it (for example STALE(rc=1,head) versus STALE(rc=1,time)). A REFUSED run has no committed sha, so the launch-time head is the only sha that exists for exactly the failing logs. ARM: a failed log with head=<old> against a newer HEAD reads STALE by head even when the commit date is older than the log mtime (GIT_COMMITTER_DATE in the past), and a log with no head line still falls back to time.

waypoints.title: A runner change must not rerun the whole mutation grid: pin the runner the grid consumes, or cut the runner into cones

ALTERNATIVES to design among: (A) github-82's: the grid consumes a PINNED runner (by commit or blob, as resumes' paperkit_engine pin does), so a runner change lands with its own unit tests and its own mutation cells (fast), and moving the grid onto the new runner is a separate reviewed repin that reruns the grid off the critical path (a pinned repoint is a software update; the grid-wide cost belongs to a repoint run); (B) split the runner into cones (the hang watcher, the control, the baseline reader, the plant writer) so a change inside one cone invalidates only the dists whose cells reach it by the import graph; the cone is measurable now with importdag cost.affected over check_mutants; (C) an interface digest: the runner publishes a content-stable behaviour digest (as W2262's diamond does for source) and a change that leaves the digest equal (a comment, a private rename) reruns nothing; (D) accept the full rerun but make it cheap (W2822 per-site targets, W2935 exclusive tag, W2460 resumable batches).
